description: Send native ETH from Ethereum and receive Tether USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Match both contracts on Etherscan and Snowtrace before you sign. You pay ETH gas.
intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. You send native ether from your Ethereum wallet and you receive Tether USDT on Avalanche C-Chain, at the address you set as the destination.

The marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means the gas coin, not an ERC-20 you can open as a token page. Ethereum is chain id 1, gas is ETH, and blocks are about 12 seconds, which you watch on Etherscan. The USDT you receive is Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Avalanche C-Chain. Confirm that contract on Snowtrace. C-Chain is chain id 43114, gas there is AVAX, and the X-Chain is outside this route.

sections.heading: Native ether is the only input
sections.body: This page spends the native ETH balance on Ethereum. It does not spend WETH, USDC, or DAI. Because the input is the gas coin, you do not sign an ERC-20 approval for the asset itself. You still leave enough ETH to pay the Ethereum fee. If your ether is already wrapped, unwrap it on Ethereum or use the WETH page instead. Buying USDT on Ethereum never creates a balance on C-Chain.

sections.heading: Tether's C-Chain contract
sections.body: The payout is Tether's dollar token, contract 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, and Snowtrace is the explorer that should list it. It is not Circle USDC and it is not the USDT contract on Ethereum. When the tokens arrive, the same wallet needs AVAX. Ether left on Ethereum cannot pay C-Chain gas. A zero AVAX balance leaves the USDT visible and immovable.

sections.heading: Skip this page for AVAX or X-Chain
sections.body: If you wanted AVAX, this route is the wrong tool, because it pays Tether. If your Avalanche address is an X-Chain address, it is also the wrong tool: settlement is C-Chain only. Staying on Ethereum is simpler when you never needed Avalanche. A short read on [how cross-chain bridges move funds](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains the wait. The quote does not lock a price or a completion time. If the minimum received is too low, do not sign.

sections.heading: Read the ETH out and the USDT floor
sections.body: Check the amount of ETH leaving Ethereum, the USDT estimated on C-Chain, and the minimum you still accept if the market moves. Network fees sit on their own line. A block near 12 seconds does not make Ethereum gas cheap, and a quicker C-Chain block does not shrink that fee. Sign on chain id 1 from a wallet you control. Do not paste a destination from a chat message.

faqs.question: Do I approve a token on Ethereum before sending ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH uses the marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which is not an ERC-20 approval. You only need enough ether for the amount you send plus the network fee. After the route, look up Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Snowtrace. Etherscan will not show that C-Chain balance.

faqs.question: Can this USDT land on Avalanche X-Chain?
faqs.answer: No. The payout is Tether on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. X-Chain does not hold this contract, and an X-Chain address will not receive it. Snowtrace is the explorer for the result. Keep a little AVAX on C-Chain so you can transfer or trade the USDT after it shows up in the wallet.

faqs.question: Is the USDT amount locked when I open the page?
faqs.answer: No. The quote is an estimate, and ether can move while Ethereum confirms and while the bridge stays open. The minimum received on the quote you sign is the floor that matters. If that number is worse than you accept, request a new quote or leave the page. Nothing here promises a fill.

description: Send native ETH from Ethereum and receive native AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. The same placeholder means a different gas coin on each chain. Check Snowtrace.
intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. You send native ether on Ethereum and you receive native AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain, which you can spend as gas there.

Both fields show 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and that marker means the gas coin of whichever chain you are on. On Ethereum, chain id 1, it means ETH, and you follow the send on Etherscan. On Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, the same string means AVAX, and you follow the arrival on Snowtrace. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. This is not the X-Chain and not a wrapped token on either side.

sections.heading: One marker, two different coins
sections.body: The placeholder is not a contract with a supply you can read. On the Ethereum side it points at the native ETH balance. On the C-Chain side it points at native AVAX. Sending ETH does not unwrap anything, and receiving AVAX does not give you WETH. If you hold only WETH, this page will not take it. If you wanted USDT or USDC, pick that payout instead of AVAX.

sections.heading: C-Chain gas arrives as the asset
sections.body: Because the payout is AVAX itself, the coins you receive can pay later C-Chain fees, once they are in the wallet. You still pay the Ethereum side in ETH, and you should not drain the wallet to zero or the send cannot be mined. Snowtrace shows C-Chain activity. An X-Chain explorer will stay empty for this route, even if the ticker looks familiar.

sections.heading: Wrong tool when you need a dollar token
sections.body: Use a different page if the destination you need is Tether or Circle USDC. AVAX moves with the market while the bridge is open, so a dollar payout is a different trade. It is also the wrong tool if you only wanted to hold ETH, or if your address is on the X-Chain. See [Avalanche C-Chain notes](/chains/avalanche) before you confuse those networks. No price and no finish time is promised.

sections.heading: What the quote is asking you to accept
sections.body: Compare the ETH you give up with the AVAX the quote estimates, then look at the minimum AVAX under that estimate. Those are not the same number. Ethereum fees can jump even when blocks keep a roughly 12 second pace. Sign only on chain id 1, and check that the wallet network matches before you confirm. Leave the page if the minimum is a smaller bag than you want.

faqs.question: Why do both addresses look identical?
faqs.answer: Routers use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as a stand-in for the native gas coin. On Ethereum that coin is ETH. On Avalanche C-Chain that coin is AVAX. Etherscan and Snowtrace are different sites because the chains are different. Do not search for that placeholder as if it were an ERC-20 token contract with holders.

faqs.question: Will I get AVAX on the X-Chain?
faqs.answer: No. This route delivers native AVAX on the C-Chain, chain id 43114. The X-Chain and the P-Chain are separate. If you paste an X-Chain address, you are using the wrong tool. Snowtrace is where the C-Chain receipt belongs. You pay ETH gas on Ethereum for the send, about a 12 second block, and the bridge wait is extra.

faqs.question: Can I undo the swap if AVAX drops while I wait?
faqs.answer: No. Once you sign and the Ethereum transaction confirms, this site cannot pull the ETH back. Price is not locked. Read the minimum AVAX on the quote and sign only if that floor is still acceptable. If the quote expires, request another one rather than trusting the old figure.

description: Send wrapped ether from Ethereum and receive Circle USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. Approve the WETH contract on Etherscan, then match that USDC on Snowtrace.
intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. You send wrapped ether, an ERC-20, from Ethereum and you receive Circle USDC on Avalanche C-Chain.

WETH lives at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. That is not native ETH, so Etherscan shows a token approval before the router can move it. Ethereum is chain id 1 and gas is still ETH, with blocks around 12 seconds. The USDC you receive is Circle's token at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Match it on Snowtrace, on C-Chain chain id 43114. Gas after arrival is AVAX, not the USDC you just received.

sections.heading: Approve WETH, then spend it
sections.body: Wrapped ether is a contract, so the wallet must approve 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 before the swap can pull it. Native ETH at the gas-coin marker will not satisfy this page. Unwrapping WETH into ETH stays on Ethereum and is a different action from bridging. Keep extra ETH beside the WETH or the approval and the swap cannot pay gas.

sections.heading: Circle USDC on Snowtrace
sections.body: The destination contract is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, Circle USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. It is not Tether, and it is not Ethereum USDC. Older bridged copies of USDC exist on Avalanche. This page names the contract above, so compare the full string on Snowtrace rather than trusting the ticker. USDC cannot pay C-Chain gas. Hold AVAX too.

sections.heading: Stay off this page to unwrap or to buy AVAX
sections.body: If you wanted native ETH in the same wallet, unwrap WETH on Ethereum. If you wanted AVAX, this payout is the wrong tool because it pays Circle's dollar token. If you wanted Tether, switch pages. A same-chain WETH to USDC trade on Ethereum also skips the bridge. The [bridge guide](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the walkthrough for the hop itself. The quote does not promise a price or a clock.

sections.heading: Approval cost and the minimum USDC
sections.body: You may pay Ethereum gas twice, once for the approval and once for the swap, and both fees are ETH. The USDC line on the quote is an estimate. The minimum is the number you are willing to accept. C-Chain being a different network does not cap the Ethereum fee. Sign with the wallet that holds the WETH, on chain id 1, and recheck the Snowtrace address if anything looks one character off.

faqs.question: Is WETH the same thing as the ETH I use for gas?
faqs.answer: No. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is an ERC-20 wrapper. Gas on Ethereum is native ETH, and you need both if this route is going to move the wrapper. Etherscan lists them separately. Unwrapping is a same-chain action and does not deliver USDC on Avalanche.

faqs.question: Which USDC contract should Snowtrace show?
faqs.answer: Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. Do not stop at the letters USDC. A bridged copy can share the ticker and still be the wrong token. You will also need AVAX in that wallet before you can move the USDC.

faqs.question: What if I only hold native ETH?
faqs.answer: This page will not take it. Native ETH uses a different route. You would wrap on Ethereum first, which is its own transaction, or you would open the native ETH page for the payout you want. Wrapping does not set a bridge price. Read a fresh quote after the wrap confirms.

description: Send wrapped ether from Ethereum and receive Tether USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. WETH is not the gas coin. Match both contracts before you sign the quote.
intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. You send wrapped ether from Ethereum and you receive Tether USDT on Avalanche C-Chain, not AVAX and not USDC.

The WETH contract is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and Etherscan is where you confirm that approval. Ethereum, chain id 1, still charges gas in ETH even though you are spending a wrapper, and blocks take about 12 seconds. Tether on the far side is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Snowtrace should show that exact contract on C-Chain, chain id 43114. Bring AVAX for gas after the USDT arrives.

sections.heading: The wrapper has to be approved
sections.body: WETH does not move just because the wallet holds it. You approve 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, then the route can transfer the amount in the quote. That approval is not a bridge by itself. Native ETH will not be pulled by this page. If the wallet has WETH and almost no ETH, the approval will sit unsent.

sections.heading: Tether, not Circle, on C-Chain
sections.body: The asset that arrives is Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Circle USDC is a different contract and a different issuer. Ethereum USDT is a different chain. Snowtrace is the check, not Etherscan, once you are looking for the payout. USDT on C-Chain still cannot pay the AVAX fee, so plan a small AVAX balance before you need to move the dollars.

sections.heading: Do not use this to unwrap or to mint AVAX
sections.body: Unwrapping WETH returns native ETH on Ethereum only. It will not produce Tether on Avalanche. If your goal is AVAX, or Circle USDC, this payout is the wrong tool. If both WETH and USDT already sit on Ethereum and you do not need C-Chain, a local swap is the smaller job. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where the WETH contract lives. The quote can expire. It does not freeze a price.

sections.heading: Two Ethereum fees, then an AVAX problem
sections.body: Budget ETH for the approval and ETH for the swap. The quote's USDT figure can change while those transactions confirm, so the minimum received is the line to trust. Nobody is promising how long the bridge portion takes after Ethereum includes your transaction. When Snowtrace shows the Tether transfer, you still need AVAX in that same destination wallet.

faqs.question: Why is gas ETH if I am paying in WETH?
faqs.answer: WETH is the asset being sold. Ethereum gas is always native ETH on chain id 1, whether the token is wrapped ether or anything else. Etherscan will show the approval and the swap as ETH-paid transactions. The WETH contract itself is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2.

faqs.question: Is C-Chain USDT the same token as Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: It is Tether's dollar token, but the contract and the chain are different. This route pays 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, which you verify on Snowtrace. Looking up Ethereum USDT on Etherscan will not show the coins this page delivers. You need AVAX afterward to move them.

faqs.question: Can I send native ETH on this page instead of WETH?
faqs.answer: No. This input is the WETH contract only. Native ETH has its own route to C-Chain USDT. Wrapping ETH into WETH is a separate Ethereum action and does not lock the later quote. If you wrap, wait for it to confirm, then price this page again.

description: Send wrapped ether from Ethereum and receive native AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. Unwrapping WETH on Ethereum is a different job. You still need AVAX after.
intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. You send wrapped ether from Ethereum and you receive native AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain, the coin that pays gas there.

WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, an ERC-20 you approve, and Etherscan is the record of that approval. Gas for the approval is native ETH on chain id 1, with blocks around 12 seconds. The AVAX side uses the marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which on C-Chain means the native gas coin, not WETH. Snowtrace is the explorer. Chain id 43114. Not the X-Chain.

sections.heading: WETH in, not the gas coin
sections.body: You must hold WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and you must approve it. The ETH you use for fees is a second balance. If someone tells you WETH and ETH are the same button on this page, they are wrong. Unwrapping WETH gives you ETH on Ethereum. It does not give you AVAX, and it does not finish this route.

sections.heading: Native AVAX uses the placeholder
sections.body: The destination string 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not a token contract on Snowtrace. On C-Chain it means native AVAX. That AVAX can pay later fees, which is different from receiving USDC or USDT, where you would still need a separate gas balance. Do not hunt for that placeholder as an ERC-20. Do not send the route to an X-Chain address.

sections.heading: Wrong when you wanted dollars or a simple unwrap
sections.body: Pick another page if you need Circle USDC or Tether. This one pays a volatile coin, and the AVAX amount can move while Ethereum is still confirming. It is also the wrong tool if you only wanted to turn WETH back into ETH. That unwrap never leaves Ethereum. Read the [C-Chain page](/chains/avalanche) if you are unsure which Avalanche network you are on. No fill time and no price is guaranteed.

sections.heading: Leave ETH for gas and judge the AVAX floor
sections.body: The approval and the swap both cost ETH. Draining ETH to wrap more WETH can stall the send. On the quote, the AVAX estimate and the minimum AVAX are different lines. Sign against the minimum. A 12 second block time is only the Ethereum pace, not a promise that AVAX is already in the wallet. Check chain id 1 in the wallet before you confirm.

faqs.question: Does receiving AVAX mean I can skip holding AVAX beforehand?
faqs.answer: The AVAX from this route can pay C-Chain gas after it arrives. You do not need a prior AVAX balance for the payout to land, but you do need ETH on Ethereum to approve WETH and to send the swap. Snowtrace shows the native AVAX credit. The marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE.

faqs.question: Why is the destination address not a normal token contract?
faqs.answer: Because native AVAX is the gas coin, and routers mark it with 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE instead of an ERC-20. WETH on the way in is a real contract, 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, which you can open on Etherscan. The two strings are supposed to look different.

faqs.question: What if I wanted USDT and opened this by mistake?
faqs.answer: Stop. This page pays AVAX, not Tether. Selling WETH for USDT on C-Chain is a different route with a different destination contract. Signing here gives you a coin that moves with the AVAX market. If the quote is still unsigned, leave and open the USDT page.

description: Send WBTC from Ethereum and receive Circle USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. WBTC is not bitcoin on the Bitcoin network. Match both contracts before you sign.
intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. You send WBTC, an Ethereum token, and you receive Circle USDC on Avalanche C-Chain.

WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is not bitcoin on the Bitcoin network. Etherscan shows it as an ERC-20, and you approve that contract before it can move. Ethereum is chain id 1, gas is ETH, and blocks are about 12 seconds. Circle USDC on C-Chain is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Match the full address on Snowtrace. Chain id 43114. Gas after that is AVAX.

sections.heading: WBTC never leaves onto Bitcoin
sections.body: This route cannot pay a Bitcoin address, and it cannot accept a Bitcoin deposit. The input is the Ethereum contract 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 only. If your coins are still on the Bitcoin chain, this page is the wrong tool until they are WBTC on Ethereum. You also need ETH for gas. WBTC itself does not pay Ethereum fees.

sections.heading: Circle's USDC, checked on Snowtrace
sections.body: The payout contract is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. That is Circle USDC on Avalanche C-Chain, not Tether, and not the USDC contract on Ethereum. Snowtrace is the explorer to use. A similar ticker on a bridged copy is not automatically this route. USDC will not pay C-Chain fees, so the destination wallet needs AVAX once you want to move the dollars.

sections.heading: Skip it if you need AVAX, Tether, or a Bitcoin payment
sections.body: AVAX and USDT are different pages. A Bitcoin invoice is not a page on this site at all. Selling WBTC for USDC on Ethereum is the better fit when you never needed C-Chain. The bridge is only justified by a balance you want on Avalanche. [How bridging works](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is worth reading before you move a large WBTC lot. The quote does not lock the USDC amount.

sections.heading: Eight-decimal WBTC and the minimum dollars
sections.body: WBTC uses eight decimals. Do not compare its raw integer with a USDC integer and call that a price. Read the human amounts on the quote, then read the minimum USDC under them. ETH gas is a separate cost and can be high on chain id 1. Sign from the wallet that holds the WBTC. If the minimum dollars are too few for the bitcoin exposure you are selling, do not sign.

faqs.question: Can I paste a Bitcoin address as the destination?
faqs.answer: No. The destination is an Avalanche C-Chain address that will hold Circle USDC at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. A Bitcoin address cannot receive that token. WBTC on the way in is 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Ethereum, which you confirm on Etherscan, not in a Bitcoin wallet.

faqs.question: Does this redeem WBTC for coins on the Bitcoin chain?
faqs.answer: No. Redemption of WBTC, if you use the issuer's own process, is not this route. This page sells the Ethereum token and delivers Circle USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. Snowtrace is where that USDC should appear. You still need AVAX to spend it.

faqs.question: What if the wallet holds a bitcoin ticker that is not this contract?
faqs.answer: Do not send it here. Only 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is the WBTC this page takes. Other tickers can copy the name. Check the full contract on Etherscan before you approve anything. An approval of the wrong token does not start this swap.

description: Send WBTC from Ethereum and receive Tether USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. This does not pay a Bitcoin address. Check Etherscan and Snowtrace before you sign.
intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. You send WBTC on Ethereum and you receive Tether USDT on Avalanche C-Chain.

The token you approve is 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599. Etherscan lists that contract on chain id 1. It is an Ethereum asset, not a Bitcoin-chain coin, and gas to move it is ETH, with blocks about 12 seconds. Tether on C-Chain is 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Snowtrace is the explorer for that payout. C-Chain is chain id 43114. You will want AVAX in the receiving wallet so the USDT is not stuck.

sections.heading: Approve the WBTC contract, not a Bitcoin wallet
sections.body: Your Bitcoin wallet cannot sign this route. The balance that matters is WBTC inside an Ethereum wallet, contract 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599. You approve that ERC-20, then the swap can take the amount. Keep ETH next to it for gas. If the only bitcoin you have is on the Bitcoin chain, stop. This page cannot see it.

sections.heading: Tether's contract on Snowtrace
sections.body: USDT here is Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Circle USDC is a different issuer and a different address. Ethereum USDT will not update when C-Chain USDT arrives. Use Snowtrace for the destination and Etherscan for the send. AVAX pays C-Chain gas. Tether does not. A wallet with USDT and no AVAX cannot make the next move.

sections.heading: The wrong tool for USDC, AVAX, or a BTC address
sections.body: Open the USDC page if you want Circle's token. Open the AVAX page if you want the gas coin. Close this page if someone asked you to pay a Bitcoin address. Selling WBTC into USDT on Ethereum is enough when Avalanche was never the point. Look through [how to bridge assets](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) if the two-chain part is new. Price and timing stay unlocked.

sections.heading: Judge the Tether floor, not the headline
sections.body: WBTC can move while you approve and while Ethereum includes the transaction. The estimate on the quote is not the promise. The minimum USDT is the number you are being asked to accept, and even that assumes the route completes. ETH gas comes off the Ethereum wallet, not off the USDT. If the floor is thin, wait for a new quote or do not sign.

faqs.question: Is WBTC going to show up as USDT on Etherscan?
faqs.answer: No. Etherscan shows the WBTC leaving Ethereum at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599. The USDT is Tether on Avalanche C-Chain, 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, and Snowtrace is where you look. They are different chains. You need AVAX after arrival. The bridge wait sits on top of the Ethereum block, and this page does not promise when those dollars show up.

faqs.question: Can this route cash WBTC out onto the Bitcoin network?
faqs.answer: No. Nothing on this page creates a Bitcoin-chain transaction. WBTC stays an Ethereum token until the route spends it, and the thing you receive is Tether on C-Chain. If your goal is bitcoin in a Bitcoin wallet, this is the wrong tool.

faqs.question: Do I need AVAX before the USDT can arrive?
faqs.answer: You need ETH on Ethereum to approve and to send. AVAX is what you need on C-Chain after Tether arrives, so you can transfer it. The payout contract does not pay gas for you. Chain id on the destination is 43114. If the quote expires before you sign, refresh it.

description: Send WBTC from Ethereum and receive native AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. You are not moving bitcoin onto the X-Chain. Match both contracts before you sign.
intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. You send WBTC on Ethereum and you receive native AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain.

WBTC is the ERC-20 at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599, which you confirm and approve on Etherscan. It is not a coin on the Bitcoin chain. Ethereum, chain id 1, charges ETH for gas and blocks in about 12 seconds. The AVAX you receive is the C-Chain gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and Snowtrace is where that native credit belongs. Chain id 43114. The X-Chain is not involved.

sections.heading: An Ethereum token with eight decimals
sections.body: Approve only 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599. Other tokens that mention bitcoin in the name are not this input. You need ETH beside the WBTC or the approval cannot be mined. A Bitcoin address cannot be the source and cannot be the destination. If that is the address you were given, leave this page.

sections.heading: AVAX arrives as the native coin
sections.body: The output marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means native AVAX on C-Chain, not a wrapped token and not USDC. Snowtrace will show a native transfer rather than an ERC-20 payout. That AVAX can pay later C-Chain fees. It is still the wrong network if you are watching the X-Chain. Ethereum ETH does not become spendable gas on Avalanche.

sections.heading: Do not use this for dollars or for Bitcoin
sections.body: Tether and Circle USDC are different routes with token contracts, not the gas-coin marker. A payment on the Bitcoin chain is outside this product. If you wanted to keep bitcoin exposure, selling WBTC into AVAX is the wrong tool because you take AVAX price risk while the bridge is open. [C-Chain basics](/chains/avalanche) help if the chain names are blurring. No price is locked.

sections.heading: Two volatile prices and an ETH fee
sections.body: You are leaving WBTC and arriving in AVAX. Both can move, so the quote's AVAX estimate is not a floor. The minimum AVAX is the floor, and you should sign only if you would still accept it. ETH gas on Ethereum is an extra cost on top. Block time near 12 seconds is not a delivery promise. Confirm the wallet says chain id 1 before the signature.

faqs.question: Does the AVAX side use a token contract I can open?
faqs.answer: The destination is the native marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which means AVAX, the gas coin, on C-Chain. It is not an ERC-20 page on Snowtrace. The input is a real contract, WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599, and that one does open on Etherscan. You approve the input only.

faqs.question: Will this send bitcoin to an Avalanche X-Chain address?
faqs.answer: No. It spends WBTC on Ethereum and delivers native AVAX on C-Chain, chain id 43114. X-Chain addresses are the wrong tool for this route. The Bitcoin network is not a hop in the middle. If Snowtrace is not the explorer you are checking, you are on the wrong screen.

faqs.question: What happens if AVAX falls after I sign?
faqs.answer: The site cannot reverse a confirmed Ethereum transaction, and it does not insure the AVAX price. That is why the minimum on the quote matters before you sign. If you need a dollar token instead of AVAX, use the USDC or USDT page. Gas for the send is still ETH.

description: Send Circle USDC on Ethereum and receive Tether USDT on Solana. Approve the contract on Etherscan, then match the SPL mint on Solscan before you sign.
intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to USDT on Solana. You send Circle USDC on Ethereum and you receive Tether USDT on Solana, in a wallet such as Phantom or Solflare.

Circle's contract on Ethereum is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. You approve that ERC-20. Etherscan shows the approval on chain id 1, gas is ETH, and blocks are about 12 seconds. Tether's SPL mint on Solana is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. Match it on Solscan. Solana does not use an ERC-20 approval. Keep a little SOL in the receiving wallet or the USDT cannot be moved.

sections.heading: Circle has to be approved first
sections.body: USDC on this page is the Ethereum token at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, issued by Circle. The wallet signs an approval, then the swap can take the amount. That approval spends ETH as gas. It does not create a Solana balance by itself. If you hold USDC on another chain, this page cannot see it. Native ETH is not an input here.

sections.heading: Tether's mint, read on Solscan
sections.body: The coins that arrive are Tether, mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. They are not Circle USDC, and they are not Ethereum USDT. Solscan is the explorer for that mint. Phantom and Solflare can hold it. An Ethereum address in an EVM wallet will not show the result. There is no ERC-20 approval on the Solana side. SOL pays the fees once you want to send the USDT onward.

sections.heading: Stay on Ethereum if the ticker change was the only goal
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you wanted USDT next to your other Ethereum tokens. A same-chain swap does that without a second wallet. It is also the wrong tool when you wanted Circle USDC on Solana, because the issuer changes to Tether. Read [Solana wallet basics](/chains/solana) if Phantom or Solflare is new. The quote does not lock a dollar amount or a finish time.

sections.heading: Minimum USDT, plus SOL for the next step
sections.body: Both tokens use six decimals, but the chains do not share a balance. Read the USDC leaving Ethereum and the minimum USDT on Solana as separate lines. ETH gas on chain id 1 can cost more than the Solana fee you will pay later. Sign the approval only for the contract above. If the minimum is below what you will accept, do not sign the swap.

faqs.question: Do I approve USDT on Solana the way I approve USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. The approval is only for Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum, and Etherscan is where that shows. Solana does not use ERC-20 approvals. You receive Tether at Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, which you check on Solscan in Phantom or Solflare. Keep a little SOL there for later fees.

faqs.question: Can an Ethereum wallet hold the USDT from this route?
faqs.answer: An Ethereum wallet can hold the USDC you send. It cannot hold the SPL USDT this page pays. The receiving wallet should be Phantom or Solflare, and the mint should be Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB on Solscan. If you paste an Ethereum address as the Solana destination, this route is the wrong tool.

faqs.question: Is the USDT I receive priced one for one with the USDC I send?
faqs.answer: No price is promised. Circle and Tether can trade slightly apart, and the bridge stays open while Ethereum confirms. Use the minimum USDT on the quote, not a mental one-for-one. If that floor is short, refresh the quote. Gas on the send is ETH, on chain id 1, and that fee is separate.

description: Send Circle USDC on Ethereum and receive SOL on Solana. Wrapped SOL is the mint on Solscan. Phantom or Solflare holds it, so match that mint before you sign.
intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to SOL on Solana. You send Circle USDC on Ethereum and you receive SOL on Solana, the coin Phantom and Solflare spend on fees.

The USDC you approve is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Ethereum. Etherscan lists that contract on chain id 1. Gas for the approval is ETH, and blocks are about 12 seconds. The Solana side is the wrapped SOL mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. Solscan is where you match that mint. It is not an ERC-20, and Solana will not ask for an ERC-20 approval. Native SOL is the gas coin those wallets already spend.

sections.heading: Dollars in, Solana's fee coin out
sections.body: You are selling Circle's dollar token and taking SOL exposure. The input contract is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. If you wanted USDT or USDC to arrive on Solana, this page is the wrong tool, because the payout is not a stablecoin. Approve only the Circle contract. Keep ETH for the Ethereum fee or the approval never broadcasts.

sections.heading: The mint Solscan should show
sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the wrapped SOL mint. Wallets often present SOL as the native balance you spend on fees. This page is aimed at that SOL destination, not at an SPL dollar mint. Solscan is the check. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. Do not search for this mint on Etherscan.

sections.heading: Wrong tool for a stable balance
sections.body: Stay off this route if you need spending dollars on Solana. USDC and USDT have their own pages. It is also the wrong tool if your USDC is already on Solana, because this input is the Ethereum contract only. [How a bridge moves assets](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the general picture. SOL's price can move the whole time. Nothing here freezes a rate.

sections.heading: Read the SOL floor before you approve
sections.body: The quote shows an estimate of SOL and a minimum under it. Sign against the minimum. A busy Ethereum block, even at about 12 seconds, can make the ETH fee larger than you expected, and that fee is separate from the SOL you receive. After arrival, the SOL itself can pay Solana fees. If the minimum SOL is too small, walk away.

faqs.question: Why is the Solana address a long mint instead of 0xEeee?
faqs.answer: Solana does not use the EVM gas-coin marker. This payout is the wrapped SOL mint So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, which you match on Solscan. Phantom and Solflare spend native SOL on fees. The USDC you send is still the Ethereum contract 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana.

faqs.question: What if I needed USDC to arrive, not SOL?
faqs.answer: Then this page is the wrong tool. It sells Circle USDC from Ethereum and pays SOL, so you take SOL price movement while the route is open. Circle USDC on Solana is a different mint and a different page. Leave this quote unsigned and open the USDC payout if dollars are what the destination wallet needs.

faqs.question: Does the SOL amount stay fixed after I see the quote?
faqs.answer: No. The quote is an estimate, and SOL can move while Ethereum confirms the USDC transfer. The minimum on that quote is the floor to judge. If it is too low, ask for a new quote. This page does not promise a fill. Gas for the send is ETH on chain id 1.

description: Send Tether USDT on Ethereum and receive Circle USDC on Solana. You change issuer and chain. Match both addresses on Etherscan and Solscan first. Then sign.
intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to USDC on Solana. You send Tether USDT on Ethereum and you receive Circle USDC on Solana.

Tether on Ethereum is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. You approve that contract, and Etherscan shows it on chain id 1. Gas is ETH, with blocks around 12 seconds. Circle's SPL USDC is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Match the full mint on Solscan. Phantom or Solflare holds the result. Solana does not use an ERC-20 approval. You need SOL in that wallet to move the USDC afterward.

sections.heading: Tether on Ethereum is an approval, not a wire
sections.body: USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 sometimes needs an old approval cleared before a new one can be set. That extra Ethereum transaction still costs ETH. This page will not take Circle USDC or DAI as the input. Native ETH is a different route. The approval alone does not credit Solana.

sections.heading: Circle's mint is the only payout
sections.body: The destination is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, Circle USDC on Solana. It is not Tether's SPL token and it is not Ethereum USDC. Solscan should show that mint and no other. An Ethereum wallet cannot display it. There is no approval step on Solana. Budget SOL for the first transfer you make after the USDC arrives.

sections.heading: Issuer change is the point, and sometimes the mistake
sections.body: You are leaving Tether and arriving in Circle's token, on a different chain. If you only needed USDC on Ethereum, this is the wrong tool. If you needed Tether on Solana, it is also the wrong tool. A same-chain swap on Ethereum avoids the wallet change. The steps in [the bridge guide](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) assume you really want the other network. No price is locked.

sections.heading: Six-decimal dollars, two explorers
sections.body: Both tokens are quoted in dollars, and both use six decimals, but the amounts live on different ledgers. Etherscan proves the USDT left. Solscan proves the USDC arrived. Read the minimum USDC before you sign. ETH gas is paid on the way out and does not come out of the Solana USDC. Refresh the quote if it expires.

faqs.question: Why did my wallet ask me to reset the USDT approval?
faqs.answer: Tether's Ethereum contract at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 often refuses to raise an existing allowance. Wallets clear it to zero, then set the new amount. Both steps cost ETH and show on Etherscan. That reset is not the bridge. The USDC you receive is still EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v on Solscan.

faqs.question: Will Solana ask me to approve USDC after it arrives?
faqs.answer: No. Solana does not use ERC-20 approvals. Phantom or Solflare will show Circle USDC at EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v once Solscan can see the mint transfer. You do need a little SOL in that wallet to pay the fee when you move the USDC. The Ethereum approval was only for the Tether you sent.

faqs.question: Can I receive Tether on Solana from this page?
faqs.answer: No. This page pays Circle, not Tether. The mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. Tether on Solana is a different route. If a desk asked you for USDT, signing here is the wrong tool. Check the minimum USDC only if Circle's token is what you meant to hold.

description: Send Tether USDT on Ethereum and receive SOL on Solana. Approve USDT on Etherscan, then match the wrapped SOL mint on Solscan before you sign. You pay ETH gas.

sections.heading: Approve Tether, keep ETH for the fee
sections.body: This input is only 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Circle USDC will not be pulled, and DAI will not be pulled. Some wallets need you to clear an old USDT approval before setting a new one. That extra transaction is still ETH gas on Ethereum. It does not move any SOL into Phantom or Solflare.

sections.heading: Wrapped SOL is the mint on the quote
sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the SPL mint Solscan lists for wrapped SOL. The gas coin in Phantom and Solflare is native SOL. This route's destination is that SOL side, not a dollar mint. Do not paste the mint into an Ethereum field, and do not look for it on Etherscan. No ERC-20 approval exists on Solana.

sections.heading: The wrong page when you still want dollars
sections.body: If the point of moving was USDC or USDT you can spend without taking SOL price risk, leave this page. Tether on Solana is a different mint and a different route. Selling USDT for SOL inside Ethereum would not fund a Solana wallet either. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only the source here. The quote can move until you sign, and it can expire.

sections.heading: A dollar token against a moving coin
sections.body: USDT is Tether's dollar token. SOL is not a dollar token. The gap can widen while Ethereum confirms, so the estimate is not a promise. The minimum SOL on the quote is the line that matters. You pay ETH to start. Once SOL is in the Solana wallet it can pay fees there. If the minimum is a pile you would regret, do not sign.

faqs.question: Is the SOL I receive the same asset as ETH?
faqs.answer: No. You send Tether on Ethereum, contract 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, and you receive SOL. The mint on Solscan is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112. ETH is only the gas coin on Ethereum, chain id 1. Phantom or Solflare spends native SOL on Solana fees. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana.

faqs.question: What if the destination I was given is an Ethereum address?
faqs.answer: Then this route is the wrong tool. SOL from this page has to land in a Solana wallet, Phantom or Solflare, not in an Ethereum account. Etherscan will show the USDT leaving. Solscan is where the wrapped SOL mint should show up. Pasting a 0x address into the Solana field will not make those networks match.

faqs.question: Does signing lock the SOL price I see right now?
faqs.answer: No. Tether can be spent at the quote, but SOL can move before the route finishes, and this page does not promise a price or a completion time. Read the minimum SOL. If the quote expires, request a new one. ETH gas on Ethereum is a separate cost from that minimum.

description: Send Maker DAI from Ethereum and receive Circle USDC on Solana. Decimals change from 18 to 6. Match both addresses before you sign the quote. You pay ETH gas.
intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDC on Solana. You send Maker's DAI on Ethereum and you receive Circle USDC on Solana.

DAI is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F, an ERC-20 with 18 decimals. You approve it. Etherscan shows that contract on chain id 1. Gas is ETH and blocks are about 12 seconds. Circle's SPL USDC is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, which uses six decimals. Match it on Solscan. Phantom or Solflare holds it. Solana has no ERC-20 approval. Keep SOL for later fees.

sections.heading: Maker's token is not Circle's token
sections.body: The wallet must contain DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. USDC and USDT on Ethereum are different issuers and will not satisfy the approval. DAI's 18 decimals mean the on-chain integer looks huge next to USDC. Read the quote in human units. You still need ETH for gas, because DAI does not pay Ethereum fees.

sections.heading: Six-decimal USDC on Solscan
sections.body: The payout mint is EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v. That is Circle USDC on Solana, not a DAI mint and not Tether. Solscan is the explorer. An 18-decimal habit from Ethereum will make a raw Solana amount look small. Trust the quote's USDC figure, then check the mint. There is no approval on Solana. SOL pays the next fee.

sections.heading: Wrong tool if you wanted DAI, Tether, or a same-chain swap
sections.body: This page will not deliver DAI on Solana. If your desk only accepts Tether, it is the wrong tool. If you wanted USDC on Ethereum, swap there and skip the bridge. The issuer changes from Maker to Circle, which matters if a venue treats them differently. See [how bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) before you move size. No completion time is promised.

sections.heading: Two decimals, one minimum
sections.body: Do not subtract the raw DAI integer from the raw USDC integer. They are scaled differently, on different chains. The minimum USDC on the quote is the floor. ETH gas comes out of the Ethereum wallet on top of that. After Solscan shows the mint transfer, you still need SOL in Phantom or Solflare. Refresh if the quote goes stale.

faqs.question: Why does my DAI balance look so much larger on-chain than the USDC quote?
faqs.answer: Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F uses 18 decimals. Circle USDC on Solana, EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v, uses six. The quote already speaks in whole tokens. Compare those figures, not the raw integers on Etherscan and Solscan. You still approve DAI on Ethereum and pay ETH gas.

faqs.question: Is this the same as swapping DAI for USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. A same-chain swap would leave Circle USDC on Ethereum. This page delivers the SPL mint on Solana, which only Phantom or Solflare can hold, and Solscan is the explorer. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. If you do not need a Solana balance, this route is the wrong tool.

faqs.question: Do I need SOL before the USDC can show up?
faqs.answer: You need ETH on Ethereum to approve DAI and to send the swap. SOL is what Phantom or Solflare spends after Circle USDC arrives, so you can move it. The mint itself does not pay fees. If the destination wallet has no SOL, the USDC can sit there. This page does not promise when it arrives.

description: Send Maker DAI from Ethereum and receive Tether USDT on Solana. Approve DAI on Etherscan, then match the SPL mint on Solscan in Phantom or Solflare. Keep SOL.
intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDT on Solana. You send Maker's DAI on Ethereum and you receive Tether USDT on Solana.

You approve DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Etherscan is where that 18-decimal token lives, on chain id 1, with ETH gas and blocks about 12 seconds. Tether's SPL mint is Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB, a six-decimal token you match on Solscan. Phantom or Solflare receives it. There is no ERC-20 approval on Solana. A little SOL has to sit in that wallet before the USDT can move again.

sections.heading: Approve Maker, not the other dollar tokens
sections.body: Only 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the input. Approving Ethereum USDT or USDC does nothing for this page. DAI can trade slightly off a dollar, so this is not a pure ticker change even before the bridge. Keep ETH for the approval. If the Ethereum wallet has DAI and no ETH, you are stuck on chain id 1.

sections.heading: Tether on Solscan uses six decimals
sections.body: Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB is the mint. It is Tether, not Circle, and not Maker. Solscan should show that string in full. A Solana account will not appear on Etherscan. No ERC-20 approval is required on the Solana side. Fees there are SOL. USDT will not pay them.

sections.heading: Skip this when the payout ticker is wrong
sections.body: Circle USDC on Solana is a different mint and a different page. Native SOL is another page. Keeping DAI on Ethereum is the right choice when no Solana venue is waiting for Tether. This route is the wrong tool in all three of those cases. The [asset bridge guide](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) covers the hop in general. Your quote still does not freeze a price.

sections.heading: The floor is USDT, the fee is ETH
sections.body: Read how much DAI leaves and how much USDT is the minimum on Solana. Those numbers already account for decimals in the quote. Do not rebuild them from raw integers. Ethereum gas is a second cost, paid in ETH, and it can be large. Sign on chain id 1 only. If Solscan later shows a different mint, you signed something else.

faqs.question: Does Maker DAI become Tether automatically because both track a dollar?
faqs.answer: No. This page sells DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F and buys Tether's Solana mint Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB. The issuers are different, the decimals are different, and the chains are different. Etherscan and Solscan will not show one shared balance. The quote's minimum is the figure to trust, not a peg you assume.

faqs.question: Which wallet signs, and which wallet receives?
faqs.answer: An Ethereum wallet approves DAI and pays ETH gas on chain id 1. Phantom or Solflare receives the USDT. Solana will not ask for an ERC-20 approval. Match Es9vMFrzaCERmJfrF4H2FYD4KCoNkY11McCe8BenwNYB on Solscan before you treat the transfer as finished. Keep SOL in the receiving wallet so the USDT can move.

faqs.question: What if I wanted Circle USDC on Solana instead?
faqs.answer: Stop before you sign. This route pays Tether, not Circle. The USDC page uses a different Solana mint. Signing here because the dollar amount looks similar is the wrong tool. DAI would still leave Ethereum, and you would hold USDT. Open the page that names USDC if that is the token the venue asked for.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimals leave Ethereum
sections.body: The contract 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is Maker DAI, not USDC and not USDT. An approval of the wrong stablecoin will not start this route. You need ETH in the same wallet for gas. DAI at 18 decimals is easy to misread if you stare at the raw amount. Use the quote's human figure instead.

sections.heading: SOL on the far side is not a stablecoin
sections.body: So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 is the wrapped SOL mint on Solscan. It is not a dollar mint. Native SOL is what Phantom and Solflare burn for fees, and this route delivers that SOL side rather than USDC or USDT. There is no ERC-20 approval step after the Ethereum transaction. Do not hunt for the mint on Etherscan.

sections.heading: The wrong tool if you need dollars on Solana
sections.body: USDC and USDT pages exist so you can arrive in Circle or Tether. This page sells that stability for SOL. It is also the wrong tool if you only wanted to hold DAI, or if your DAI is not on Ethereum. [Solana](/chains/solana) is the network that will hold the result. Price is not locked while you wait, and no finish time is promised.

sections.heading: Two kinds of movement in one quote
sections.body: DAI can drift from a dollar, and SOL can move a lot, while Ethereum is still producing a block about every 12 seconds. Treat the minimum SOL as the only number you are willing to accept. ETH gas is extra. Once the SOL is in the Solana wallet, it can pay fees there. If the floor looks poor, request a new quote or leave.

faqs.question: Does this page keep me in a dollar token on Solana?
faqs.answer: No. You send Maker DAI, 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F, and you receive SOL. The mint is So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 on Solscan. If you need Circle USDC or Tether after the hop, this is the wrong tool. Phantom or Solflare will show SOL, which can pay Solana fees once it arrives.

faqs.question: Do I approve SOL on Solana after the Ethereum transaction?
faqs.answer: No. Solana does not use ERC-20 approvals. The only approval is for DAI on Ethereum, visible on Etherscan, and that approval spends ETH as gas. The wrapped SOL mint is the payout, not a token you approve. Native SOL in Phantom or Solflare is what later transactions spend as the fee.

faqs.question: Can the route be reversed if SOL drops before I see it?
faqs.answer: No. A confirmed Ethereum send is not something this site can undo, and the price is not insured. Read the minimum SOL before you sign. If that floor is already worse than you want, do not sign. Gas on the way out is ETH on chain id 1, whether or not you like the later SOL price.

description: Send native ETH from Ethereum and receive Circle USDC on Solana. No ERC-20 approval on the ETH. Match the SPL mint on Solscan before you sign. Keep some SOL.

Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on Solana. You send native ETH on Ethereum and you receive Circle USDC on Solana.

Solana has no ERC-20 approval. You will want SOL already there so the new USDC is not stuck.

sections.heading: Native ETH, not the wrapper
sections.body: This page takes the ETH balance, the same coin that pays gas, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. It does not take WETH. Leave enough ETH to cover both the amount you swap and the fee. If the wallet holds only WETH, open the WETH route or unwrap first. Unwrapping stays on Ethereum and does not create Solana USDC.

sections.heading: Circle's SPL mint
sections.body: EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v is the USDC you should see on Solscan. It is Circle, not Tether, and not Ethereum USDC. An Ethereum account will not display that mint. Phantom or Solflare will. There is no approval on Solana. SOL, not USDC, pays Solana fees, so an empty SOL balance stalls the next transfer.

sections.heading: Wrong tool for SOL, USDT, or a same-chain buy
sections.body: If you wanted SOL itself, this payout is the wrong tool. If you wanted Tether, switch pages. If you only needed USDC on Ethereum, buy it there and do not bridge. WETH holders should not force this native route. A plain account of [how to bridge](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) helps with the wallet change. The quote does not promise the USDC amount.

sections.heading: Fee coin and payout coin are different
sections.body: You pay ETH on Ethereum and you receive USDC on Solana. The USDC cannot refund your Ethereum gas. Read the minimum USDC, not just the estimate. A 12 second block is the Ethereum pace, not a delivery clock for Solscan. Sign from the wallet that holds the ETH, on chain id 1. Ignore destination addresses sent to you in a private message.

faqs.question: Do I approve ETH before this Solana USDC swap?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH uses the marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which is not an ERC-20. You only need enough ETH for the swap and for gas on chain id 1. Etherscan shows that native send. The USDC arrives as EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v on Solscan. Solana does not ask for an ERC-20 approval.

faqs.question: I hold WETH. Can I use this page anyway?
faqs.answer: No. WETH is a different contract and a different route. This page spends the native gas coin only. Unwrapping WETH on Ethereum gives you ETH in the same wallet, and that unwrap is not a bridge to Solana. After you unwrap, open a fresh quote.
