intro:
Swap ETH from BNB Chain to USDT on Polygon. You send Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain and you receive Tether USDT on Polygon.

Approve 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. BscScan lists that peg on chain id 56. Gas is BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. The peg is not BNB. Tether on Polygon is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Match it on Polygonscan. Chain id 137. POL pays the fees there. USDT does not. Ethereum USDT is a different contract on a different explorer.

sections.heading: Approve the peg, leave BNB for the fee
sections.body: The ETH ticker on BNB Chain is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. This route will not spend your BNB balance except as gas. If the peg balance is zero, stop. Native ETH on Ethereum is not an input either. The approval is a BNB Chain transaction, chain id 56, and it does not credit Polygon by itself.

sections.heading: Polygon Tether is its own contract
sections.body: 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F is what Polygonscan should show. It is not Circle's native USDC and not Ethereum USDT. Six decimals versus the peg's 18 is a display gap, not a missing fee. Read the quote. Hold POL in the same wallet or the USDT cannot be forwarded.

sections.heading: Native USDC, POL, and WETH are other pages
sections.body: If the desk asked for Circle, this Tether payout is the wrong tool. If you needed POL to pay gas, it is the wrong tool. If you meant to sell BNB, it is the wrong input. [How bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the background for the wait. No USDT figure is promised.

sections.heading: BscScan out, Polygonscan in
sections.body: Watch the peg leave on BscScan. Watch Tether arrive on Polygonscan. Etherscan is the wrong site for both. A 3 second BNB Chain block is not a Polygon finish time. Read the minimum USDT before you sign. If the floor is poor, do not sign, and do not reuse a destination address from a chat. POL still has to be waiting in that wallet.

faqs.question: Does the ETH name mean I receive ETH on Polygon?
faqs.answer: No. You send the peg 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and you receive Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. BscScan shows the send. Polygonscan shows the USDT. POL is a separate coin you need for gas on chain id 137. BNB paid only the source fee. POL is extra.

faqs.question: Is this the USDT contract from Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether lives on chain id 1. This mint is Polygon only, 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Check Polygonscan, not Etherscan. If you paste an Ethereum address and expect this USDT, the route is the wrong tool. Keep POL beside the token after it arrives.

faqs.question: Will the 18-decimal peg match USDT one for one on-chain?
faqs.answer: Do not compare raw integers. The peg uses 18 decimals and Polygon USDT uses 6. The quote speaks in whole tokens. The minimum there is the floor, and this page does not promise a price. BNB Chain blocks near 3 seconds do not lock that minimum.

description: Send Binance-Peg ETH from BNB Chain and receive WETH on Polygon. These contracts differ, and WETH cannot pay POL gas. Check BscScan and Polygonscan now.
intro:
Swap ETH from BNB Chain to WETH on Polygon. You send Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain and you receive WETH on Polygon.

The source is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Approve it on BscScan, chain id 56, gas in BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. Polygon WETH is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Match it on Polygonscan. It is not the peg, not native POL, and not Ethereum mainnet WETH. Chain id 137 charges gas in POL. The wrapper you receive cannot pay that charge.

sections.heading: Three ether tickers, one of them is the input
sections.body: BNB Chain's peg, Polygon's WETH, and Ethereum's WETH are three contracts. This page spends only 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. It does not spend BNB, and it does not wrap native ETH on Ethereum. If the peg balance is empty, there is nothing to approve. Keep BNB for gas on chain id 56.

sections.heading: Polygon WETH still needs a POL balance
sections.body: 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 arriving does not top up POL. Polygonscan will show a token, not a native credit. Every later move costs POL. A fresh Polygon wallet can display WETH and still fail a transfer. BNB left on BNB Chain does not become that POL.

sections.heading: POL is the page that pays the gas coin
sections.body: If you wanted spendable gas on Polygon, this wrapper is the wrong tool. Native USDC and USDT are the wrong tool if you wanted dollars. Selling BNB is a different input. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is only where the peg sits. The quote does not promise how much WETH lands.

sections.heading: Do not drain BNB to buy a larger peg
sections.body: The fee and the trade are different balances. Draining BNB stalls the approval. Read the minimum WETH before you sign on chain id 56. A 3 second block is not a Polygonscan timestamp. If the floor is a smaller wrapper than you will accept, leave the quote unsigned. Mainnet WETH will not update when this Polygon balance does. Keep POL in the destination the whole time.

faqs.question: Are the peg and Polygon WETH the same token on two chains?
faqs.answer: No. The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. Polygon WETH is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. Mainnet WETH is a third address. This page pays the Polygon contract only. You need BNB to send and POL, the gas coin on chain id 137, to move the result.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap this WETH into POL?
faqs.answer: No. Unwrapping WETH, where a pool offers it, does not turn the wrapper into POL. POL is the native gas coin, and this route does not pay it. If you needed POL, open that page. If you unwrap later, the fee is still POL you must already hold.

faqs.question: What if I meant to send BNB instead of the peg?
faqs.answer: Stop. BNB is the gas coin and has its own route to Polygon WETH. Approving 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 will not spend BNB. Check the native balance on BscScan. This page is the wrong tool for a BNB sale, even though the payout contract would look similar on a different route.

description: Send Binance-Peg ETH from BNB Chain and receive native POL on Polygon. The peg is not BNB. POL is the gas coin. Check BscScan and Polygonscan before you sign.
intro:
Swap ETH from BNB Chain to POL on Polygon. You send Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain and you receive native POL on Polygon.

Approve 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. BscScan shows that peg on chain id 56. Gas for the approval is BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. The peg is not the gas coin. On Polygon the marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means POL. Polygonscan shows the native credit, chain id 137. That POL can pay later fees. It is not WETH and not a dollar token.

sections.heading: The peg is sold, BNB only pays
sections.body: This input is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and nothing else. A wallet full of BNB and empty of the peg cannot use the page. You still need some BNB so the approval is mined. The trade takes POL price risk. If you wanted USDC or USDT on Polygon, you are on the wrong payout.

sections.heading: POL is the native marker on chain id 137
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not an ERC-20 on Polygonscan. Here it means POL. The same marker on BNB Chain would mean BNB, which is not what you are sending. The received POL can pay Polygon fees, so you do not need a prior POL balance for the credit to be usable.

sections.heading: WETH and dollar tokens if POL was a mistake
sections.body: Polygon WETH is a contract, not this marker. Native USDC and USDT are contracts too. Open those pages if that is what the destination needs. The [bridge guide](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) explains the hop in general. It does not lock the POL amount, and a fast BNB Chain block is not a completion time.

sections.heading: Switch the wallet to Polygon before you look
sections.body: BscScan will show the peg leaving chain id 56. The POL will not appear there. Set the wallet to chain id 137 and use Polygonscan. Read the minimum POL before you sign. If you would not hold that much POL against the peg you are selling, do not sign.

faqs.question: Does the ETH ticker on BNB Chain turn into POL one for one?
faqs.answer: No. You sell the peg at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, and the quote prices it into POL. The destination marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which means POL on Polygonscan. Nothing locks that price. Gas on the send is BNB, on chain id 56. BNB is only the fee.

faqs.question: Will I still need extra POL after this route?
faqs.answer: The payout is POL, so it can pay fees once it arrives. You do not need a prior POL balance for that. You do need BNB to approve the peg. Polygonscan shows a native credit, not WETH. If you wanted WETH specifically, this page is the wrong tool.

faqs.question: Can I send BNB on this page and still get POL?
faqs.answer: Not on this page. BNB uses the gas-coin marker as the input and has a separate route. This page approves 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 only. If BscScan shows BNB and no peg, stop. Signing an empty approval does not start the swap. Look twice.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive native Circle USDC on Polygon. No approval on the BNB. Match the USDC contract on Polygonscan and keep POL for gas.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to USDC on Polygon. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive Circle's native USDC on Polygon.

The source marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means BNB, the gas coin on chain id 56. No ERC-20 approval. BscScan shows a native send. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Leave extra BNB for the fee. Native USDC on Polygon is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Match it on Polygonscan, chain id 137. It is not USDC.e. You will need POL to move it.

sections.heading: BNB is spent as the asset and as the fee
sections.body: There is no token approval, but there is a fee. If you sell every BNB, the transaction cannot be mined. The page will not sell the ETH peg at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and will not sell a stablecoin peg. If those are the balances you meant, this is the wrong route.

sections.heading: Circle's native contract, then a POL problem
sections.body: Polygonscan should show 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 and not a bridged USDC.e address. The USDC cannot pay gas on chain id 137. POL has to be there already. BNB does not arrive with the dollars. A wallet that only holds this USDC is stuck until POL is added.

sections.heading: The peg ETH token will not be pulled
sections.body: People see ETH in the token list and assume this BNB page uses it. It does not. USDT and WETH payouts are different pages. POL as a payout is a different page. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the destination. If you only needed USDC on BNB Chain, do not bridge. No amount is locked.

sections.heading: Split the BNB before you sign
sections.body: Keep a fee remainder, then read the minimum USDC for the rest. A 3 second block on chain id 56 is not a promise that Polygonscan has the token. Sign the native send only while the wallet says BNB Chain. Reject destinations you did not generate yourself. Native USDC still cannot pay the Polygon fee by itself.

faqs.question: Do I approve BNB the way I approve the USDC peg?
faqs.answer: No. Native BNB uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which is not an ERC-20. BscScan shows a native transfer on chain id 56. You only leave extra BNB for gas. The USDC you receive is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan. That token needs POL before it can move.

faqs.question: Which USDC should Polygonscan show?
faqs.answer: Native Circle USDC, 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, on chain id 137. Bridged USDC.e is a different contract, and this route is the wrong tool if a pool demands that copy. Do not stop at the letters USDC. You still need POL in the wallet. BNB paid only the source side.

faqs.question: Can the route finish if I spend my last BNB?
faqs.answer: No. The fee comes from the same native balance you are selling. Leave enough BNB for gas on chain id 56. A failed send does not create USDC on Polygon. This page also does not promise a price or a completion time once a valid send does go through.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive Tether USDT on Polygon. BNB needs no approval. Match the USDT contract on Polygonscan and keep POL for later fees.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to USDT on Polygon. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive Tether USDT on Polygon.

0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on the source means BNB. No ERC-20 approval. BscScan records the native send on chain id 56, blocks about 3 seconds. Keep BNB for the fee. Tether on Polygon is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Match it on Polygonscan. Chain id 137. USDT will not pay POL gas, so the destination needs POL already.

sections.heading: The gas coin is the thing you sell
sections.body: This page takes native BNB only. The ETH peg and the USDT peg on BNB Chain stay put. There is no approval step for BNB, which surprises people who just approved a token on another page. You still cannot spend the last BNB, because the network fee has to fit in the remainder.

sections.heading: Tether on Polygon is not Ethereum Tether
sections.body: Match 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan. Etherscan will not show this payout. It is Tether, not Circle's native USDC. Six decimals are expected. The token does not include POL. Add POL or the USDT sits in a wallet that cannot pay for a transfer.

sections.heading: USDC and POL if Tether was not the ask
sections.body: Circle's native USDC is a different contract. POL is the gas-coin payout, a different page. The ETH peg is a different input. If you wanted USDT without leaving BNB Chain, buy it there. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the network you are leaving. The quote does not freeze the Tether amount.

sections.heading: Source speed is not the whole route
sections.body: Chain id 56 can move in about 3 seconds. That fact does not time Polygonscan and does not lock a price. Read the minimum USDT. Sign only on BNB Chain. When you later look for the tokens, the wallet has to be on chain id 137, and it has to hold POL. A wallet on the wrong chain will look empty even after a successful route.

faqs.question: Why does the BNB address look like an ETH placeholder?
faqs.answer: Routers use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for the gas coin of the chain in front of you. On BNB Chain that is BNB, and BscScan shows a native send. The payout is not that marker. It is Tether, 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, on Polygonscan. There is no ERC-20 approval on the BNB.

faqs.question: Does Polygon USDT use 18 decimals like BNB Chain USDT?
faqs.answer: No. The USDT this page pays is the Polygon contract, and you should read the quote rather than a raw integer. BNB Chain's own USDT peg is 18 decimals, and this route is not spending that peg. You still need POL on chain id 137 to move the Tether after it arrives.

faqs.question: What if the quote says USDT but I needed USDC?
faqs.answer: Do not sign. This route pays Tether only, contract 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Native USDC is a different page from the same BNB balance. Treating them as interchangeable is the wrong tool. Check Polygonscan before you send the tokens to anyone else. POL is required.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive WETH on Polygon. WETH cannot pay POL gas. Match the Polygon WETH contract on Polygonscan before you sign now.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to WETH on Polygon. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive WETH on Polygon, not POL.

The BNB side is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin on chain id 56. No ERC-20 approval. BscScan shows the native send. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Leave BNB for the fee. Polygon WETH is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Match it on Polygonscan. It is not mainnet WETH and not the BNB Chain ETH peg. Chain id 137 still wants POL for every later move.

sections.heading: Selling BNB, buying a Polygon wrapper
sections.body: Native BNB is the input. The peg at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is not. If your ether exposure on BNB Chain is only that peg, this page cannot see it. There is no approval for BNB, but the fee still comes out of BNB. Do not zero the balance and expect the swap to squeeze through.

sections.heading: The wrapper cannot pay Polygon
sections.body: 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 is an ERC-20. POL is the native coin. Polygonscan lists them apart. Receiving WETH does not give you POL, so a new wallet gets a token it cannot move. Mainnet WETH on Etherscan is a different address and will not update.

sections.heading: Open the POL page if you needed gas
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the point was a spendable Polygon balance. USDC and USDT pages are the wrong tool when you wanted dollars. [How bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) covers the wait between BscScan and Polygonscan. It does not promise a WETH amount.

sections.heading: Minimum WETH, remainder BNB, POL waiting
sections.body: Three numbers matter: the minimum WETH on the quote, the BNB you keep for chain id 56, and the POL already on chain id 137. A 3 second source block does not replace any of them. Sign only if the WETH floor is acceptable. If the quote expired, price it again. POL is not included in the WETH credit.

faqs.question: Will Polygon WETH show up as POL in the wallet?
faqs.answer: No. POL is the gas coin. WETH is the token at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. The BNB you sent was the marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on BscScan. They stay different. You need POL already in the Polygon wallet if you want to transfer the WETH.

faqs.question: Is this the same WETH address Ethereum uses?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH is a mainnet contract on Etherscan. This payout is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on chain id 137. Matching the ticker is not enough. You also need BNB left over for the source fee. There is no ERC-20 approval on the BNB itself.

faqs.question: What if the only ether I hold on BNB Chain is the peg?
faqs.answer: This page will not spend it. The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and has its own route to Polygon WETH. You need native BNB here, both to sell and to pay gas. If BscScan shows dust BNB, the route cannot start. Open the peg page instead.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive native POL on Polygon. The same marker is a different gas coin on each chain. Check BscScan and Polygonscan.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to POL on Polygon. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive native POL on Polygon.

Both sides use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On BNB Chain, chain id 56, the marker is BNB. On Polygon, chain id 137, it is POL. BscScan shows the BNB leaving. Polygonscan shows the POL arriving. There is no ERC-20 approval on either gas coin. Blocks on BNB Chain are about 3 seconds. This is not WETH, not the ETH peg, and not a dollar token.

sections.heading: One placeholder, BNB leaving and POL arriving
sections.body: The string is not a coin that hops. It means whichever gas coin the chain uses. You sell BNB and you buy POL. Both can move. The Binance-Peg ETH contract is not an input. If that is all you hold, this page will not take it. Leave some BNB, or the source fee fails.

sections.heading: Received POL can pay Polygon fees
sections.body: Because the payout is the gas coin, you do not need old POL in the wallet for the new balance to be usable. That is the difference from landing in USDC, USDT, or WETH. Polygonscan will not show an ERC-20 page for this credit. Do not search the marker as if it had holders.

sections.heading: Dollar tokens and WETH if you did not want POL
sections.body: Those payouts are other pages from the same BNB balance. This one is the wrong tool if a desk asked for Tether or Circle, or if a pool asked for Polygon WETH. The [bridge guide](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the hop, not a BNB to POL rate. Nothing freezes the amount.

sections.heading: Read the POL floor on a moving pair
sections.body: The estimate and the minimum are different lines. Sign against the minimum. A 3 second block on chain id 56 does not freeze POL. Confirm the wallet network before the signature, then look for the result on Polygonscan with chain id 137 selected. If the floor is too small, do not sign.

faqs.question: Why are the two addresses identical if BNB and POL differ?
faqs.answer: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE stands in for the native gas coin. BscScan's native coin on chain id 56 is BNB. Polygonscan's native coin on chain id 137 is POL. There is no ERC-20 approval on either side. The ETH peg on BNB Chain is a separate token and is not part of this route.

faqs.question: Do I need POL in the wallet before the swap?
faqs.answer: No. The POL from this route can pay fees after it arrives. You do need BNB left on chain id 56 to pay the source fee. If you spend the entire BNB balance, the send cannot be mined and no POL is created. Polygonscan is where the native credit belongs.

faqs.question: Can I undo the swap if POL falls after I sign?
faqs.answer: No. A confirmed BNB transfer is not reversed here, and the price is not insured. Read the minimum POL first. The 3 second block is only BNB Chain. It is not a promise about how much POL Polygonscan will show, or about when that credit appears.

description: Send Binance-Peg USDC from BNB Chain and receive Tether USDT on Arbitrum One. Gas there is ETH, not ARB. Match both contracts on BscScan and Arbiscan.
intro:
Swap USDC from BNB Chain to USDT on Arbitrum One. You send Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain and you receive Tether USDT on Arbitrum One, not on Arbitrum Nova.

Approve 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. BscScan lists that 18-decimal peg on chain id 56. Gas is BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. Tether on Arbitrum One is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Match it on Arbiscan. Chain id 42161. Gas there is ETH. The ARB token does not pay it, and neither does this USDT.

sections.heading: Peg USDC leaves chain id 56
sections.body: The only input is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Native BNB and the USDT peg will not be pulled. Keep BNB for the approval. Eighteen decimals will look huge next to Arbitrum USDT. Read the quote in whole tokens. A trade that stays on BNB Chain never creates a balance Arbiscan can show.

sections.heading: Tether on Arbiscan, ETH for the next fee
sections.body: 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 is Tether on Arbitrum One. It is not Circle's native USDC and not Ethereum mainnet USDT. Arbiscan is the explorer, and Nova is a different network that will not show this contract. You need ETH on chain id 42161 after arrival. USDT cannot pay that gas.

sections.heading: Wrong network, wrong dollar, wrong gas token
sections.body: Nova is the wrong tool. So is a page that pays native ETH, WETH, or the ARB token, if you needed Tether. So is a same-chain swap when you never needed Arbitrum. [Arbitrum](/chains/arbitrum) here means Arbitrum One. The quote does not lock a USDT amount, and a 3 second BNB Chain block is not a delivery clock.

sections.heading: BNB on the way out, ETH on the way forward
sections.body: Budget BNB for chain id 56 and ETH for chain id 42161. The minimum USDT is the floor. Sign only while the wallet says BNB Chain. When you look for the result, the wallet must say Arbitrum One, not Nova and not Ethereum. Do not paste a destination from a message.

faqs.question: Will this USDT show up on Arbitrum Nova?
faqs.answer: No. This route pays Tether on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, contract 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Arbiscan is the explorer. Nova is a different chain. The token you send is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan. Gas out is BNB. Gas on Arbitrum One is ETH, not the ARB token.

faqs.question: Can the ARB token in my wallet pay the Arbitrum fee?
faqs.answer: No. ARB is a separate token. Gas on Arbitrum One is ETH. This page does not pay you that ETH. It pays USDT. If the destination has USDT and no ETH, the dollars sit still. BNB left on BNB Chain does not cover the Arbitrum fee either.

faqs.question: Does a fast BNB Chain confirmation lock the USDT?
faqs.answer: No. Blocks near 3 seconds are only chain id 56. This page does not promise a price or a completion time. Read the minimum USDT. If it is too low, refresh the quote. You still need ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, after Arbiscan shows the Tether.

description: Send Binance-Peg USDC from BNB Chain and receive native ETH on Arbitrum One. That ETH pays gas. This is not Nova and not WETH. Check BscScan and Arbiscan.
intro:
Swap USDC from BNB Chain to ETH on Arbitrum One. You send Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain and you receive native ETH on Arbitrum One, the coin that pays gas there.

Approve 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. BscScan shows the 18-decimal peg on chain id 56. Gas is BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. The payout marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means ETH on Arbitrum One, not BNB and not WETH. Arbiscan shows the native balance. Chain id 42161. Nova is not this network. The ETH you receive can pay later fees.

sections.heading: A dollar peg buys Arbitrum's gas coin
sections.body: You sell 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d and take ETH price exposure. USDT and the ARB token are different pages. If you wanted a dollar balance on Arbitrum One, this payout is the wrong tool. Keep BNB so the approval can be mined. The peg's decimals should be read from the quote, not from a raw integer.

sections.heading: The marker is ETH, and Nova will not see it
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not an ERC-20 on Arbiscan. On chain id 42161 it means native ETH. The same string on BNB Chain would mean BNB, which is not the input. A Nova wallet is the wrong place to look. This ETH can pay gas, which is different from receiving USDT, USDC, WETH, or ARB.

sections.heading: WETH and the ARB token are separate balances
sections.body: Pools that want the WETH contract need the other page. The ARB token cannot be what this quote pays, and it cannot pay gas either.
