faqs.question: Is this the USDT contract from Ethereum mainnet?
faqs.answer: No. Mainnet Tether lives on chain id 1. This contract is Arbitrum One only. Check Arbiscan, not Etherscan. If you paste a mainnet address and expect this USDT, the route is the wrong tool. Keep ETH beside the token after it arrives. The ARB token will not pay the fee.

faqs.question: Will the peg's 18 decimals match USDT one for one?
faqs.answer: Do not compare raw integers. The peg uses 18 decimals and this USDT uses 6. The quote speaks in whole tokens. The minimum there is the floor, and this page does not promise a price. BNB Chain blocks near 3 seconds do not lock that minimum.

description: Send Binance-Peg ETH from BNB Chain and receive WETH on Arbitrum One. These are different contracts. WETH cannot pay gas. Check BscScan and Arbiscan now.
intro:
Swap ETH from BNB Chain to WETH on Arbitrum One. You send Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain and you receive WETH on Arbitrum One.

The source is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Approve it on BscScan, chain id 56, gas in BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. Arbitrum One WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Match it on Arbiscan. It is not the peg, not native ETH, and not mainnet WETH. Chain id 42161, not Nova. Gas is ETH. The wrapper cannot pay that gas. The ARB token cannot either.

sections.heading: One peg in, a different wrapper out
sections.body: This page spends only 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. It does not spend BNB, and it does not wrap ETH that already sits on Arbitrum. If the peg balance is empty, there is nothing to approve. Keep BNB for gas on chain id 56. The names both say ether. The contracts do not match.

sections.heading: Arbitrum WETH still needs a native ETH balance
sections.body: 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 arriving does not top up ETH. Arbiscan shows a token, not a native credit. Every later move costs ETH. A fresh wallet can display WETH and still fail a transfer. BNB left behind does not become that ETH. Nova will not show the balance.

sections.heading: Native ETH is the page that pays the gas coin
sections.body: If you wanted spendable gas, this wrapper is the wrong tool. Native USDC and USDT are the wrong tool if you wanted dollars. The ARB token is the wrong tool if you wanted the governance token. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is only where the peg sits. No WETH amount is promised.

sections.heading: Do not drain BNB to enlarge the peg
sections.body: The fee and the trade are different balances. Draining BNB stalls the approval. Read the minimum WETH before you sign on chain id 56. A 3 second block is not an Arbiscan timestamp. If the floor is too small, leave the quote unsigned. Nova is the wrong network for this wrapper, chain id 42161.

faqs.question: Are the peg and Arbitrum WETH the same token?
faqs.answer: No. The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. Arbitrum WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbiscan, chain id 42161. Mainnet WETH is a third address. This page pays the Arbitrum contract only. You need BNB to send and ETH to move the result. Nova is not the chain.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap this WETH into the ARB token?
faqs.answer: No. Unwrapping, where a pool offers it, returns native ETH and still costs ETH as gas. It does not mint ARB. If you needed the gas coin, open the native ETH page. If you needed ARB, open that page. This route pays the wrapper only.

faqs.question: What if I meant to send BNB, not the peg?
faqs.answer: Stop. BNB is the gas coin and has its own route to Arbitrum WETH. Approving 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 will not spend BNB. Check the native balance on BscScan. This page is the wrong tool for a BNB sale, even when the payout ticker looks like ether.

description: Send Binance-Peg ETH from BNB Chain and receive ARB on Arbitrum One. ARB does not pay gas. Match both contracts on BscScan and Arbiscan before you sign.
intro:
Swap ETH from BNB Chain to ARB on Arbitrum One. You send Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain and you receive the ARB token on Arbitrum One.

Approve 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. BscScan shows that peg on chain id 56. Gas for the approval is BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. The peg is not the gas coin. ARB is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Match it on Arbiscan. Chain id 42161, not Nova. ARB cannot pay gas. You need ETH in the receiving wallet or the token cannot move.

sections.heading: The peg is sold for the governance token
sections.body: This input is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and nothing else. A wallet full of BNB and empty of the peg cannot use the page. You still need BNB so the approval is mined. You take ARB price risk. If you wanted USDC, USDT, or native ETH, you are on the wrong payout.

sections.heading: ARB on Arbiscan is not fee ETH
sections.body: 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is a token. ETH is the native coin on chain id 42161. Receiving ARB does not top up ETH. Nova will not show this One balance. If you were told the ticker pays gas, that advice does not fit Arbitrum One.

sections.heading: Switch pages for dollars or for gas
sections.body: Native ETH, WETH, native USDC, and USDT are different routes from this peg. The [bridge guide](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) explains the hop. It does not lock the ARB amount, and a fast BNB Chain block is not a completion time. Stay on BNB Chain if you did not need ARB.

sections.heading: Plan ETH on One before you approve
sections.body: The destination needs ETH already, or the ARB token sits. Read the minimum ARB before you sign on chain id 56. Then use Arbiscan on chain id 42161. If the wallet is on Nova, you are on the wrong network even when the ticker matches. You still need native ETH on chain id 42161 after Arbiscan shows the new ARB token.

faqs.question: Does the ETH ticker on BNB Chain become ARB one for one?
faqs.answer: No. You sell the peg at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, and the quote prices it into ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Nothing locks that price. Gas on the send is BNB. Gas after arrival is ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, which this page does not pay you. Nova is not the destination.

faqs.question: Will the ARB I receive pay the next transaction?
faqs.answer: No. ARB cannot pay gas. You need ETH on chain id 42161 to move 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Arbiscan lists them apart. You also need BNB to approve the peg. If you wanted the gas coin itself, this page is the wrong tool.

faqs.question: Can I send BNB on this page and still receive ARB?
faqs.answer: Not here. BNB has a separate route. This page approves 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 only. If BscScan shows BNB and no peg, stop. An approval of the wrong asset does not start the swap, and it does not change the payout into ETH.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive native Circle USDC on Arbitrum One. No approval on the BNB. Match the USDC contract on Arbiscan and keep ETH for gas.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to USDC on Arbitrum One. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive Circle's native USDC on Arbitrum One.

The source marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means BNB, the gas coin on chain id 56. No ERC-20 approval. BscScan shows a native send. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Leave extra BNB for the fee. Native USDC is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Match it on Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. It is not USDC.e. You will need ETH to move it. ARB will not pay that fee.

sections.heading: BNB is both the asset and the fee
sections.body: There is no token approval, but there is a fee. Selling every BNB stalls the transaction. The page will not sell the ETH peg and will not sell a stablecoin peg. If those are the balances you meant, this is the wrong route. The marker is the gas coin, not a contract you open on BscScan.

sections.heading: Circle's native contract, then an ETH gap
sections.body: Arbiscan should show 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 and not a bridged USDC.e address. The USDC cannot pay gas on chain id 42161. ETH has to be there already. BNB does not arrive with the dollars. A wallet that only holds this USDC is stuck until ETH is added.

sections.heading: The peg and the ARB token are not this trade
sections.body: The ETH listing on BNB Chain is a peg this page ignores. ARB, WETH, and USDT payouts are different pages. [Arbitrum](/chains/arbitrum) is One, not Nova. If you only needed USDC on BNB Chain, do not bridge. No Circle amount is locked.

sections.heading: Split the BNB, then read the USDC floor
sections.body: Keep a fee remainder, then read the minimum USDC. A 3 second block on chain id 56 is not a promise that Arbiscan has the token. Sign while the wallet says BNB Chain. Look for the result on chain id 42161. Reject destinations you did not generate. Stay off Nova.

faqs.question: Do I approve BNB before this Arbitrum USDC swap?
faqs.answer: No. Native BNB uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which is not an ERC-20. BscScan shows a native transfer on chain id 56. You only leave extra BNB for gas. The USDC you receive is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan. That token needs ETH on Arbitrum One before it can move.

faqs.question: Which USDC should Arbiscan show?
faqs.answer: Native Circle USDC, 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, on chain id 42161. Bridged USDC.e is a different contract. If a pool wants that copy, this route is the wrong tool. Nova will not show the One balance. You still need ETH. The ARB token does not pay the fee.

faqs.question: What happens if I spend my last BNB?
faqs.answer: The fee comes from the same native balance you are selling. Leave enough BNB for gas on chain id 56 or the send cannot be mined and no USDC appears. This page also does not promise a price or a completion time once a valid send does go through.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive Tether USDT on Arbitrum One. BNB needs no approval. Match the USDT contract on Arbiscan and keep ETH for later fees.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to USDT on Arbitrum One. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive Tether USDT on Arbitrum One.

0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on the source means BNB. No ERC-20 approval. BscScan records the native send on chain id 56, blocks about 3 seconds. Keep BNB for the fee. Tether on Arbitrum One is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Match it on Arbiscan. Chain id 42161, not Nova. USDT will not pay ETH gas, and the ARB token will not either.

sections.heading: You sell the gas coin, not a peg
sections.body: This page takes native BNB only. The ETH peg and the USDT peg on BNB Chain stay put. There is no approval step for BNB. You still cannot spend the last BNB, because the network fee has to fit in the remainder. If the balance you meant was the peg, open that page instead.

sections.heading: Tether on One is not mainnet Tether
sections.body: Match 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan. Etherscan will not show this payout, and Nova will not either. It is Tether, not Circle's native USDC. The token does not include ETH. Add ETH or the USDT sits in a wallet that cannot pay for a transfer.

sections.heading: USDC, ETH, and ARB if Tether was not the ask
sections.body: Circle's native USDC is a different contract. Native ETH is the gas-coin payout. ARB is the governance token. The ETH peg is a different input. If you wanted USDT without leaving BNB Chain, buy it there. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is what you are leaving. The quote does not freeze the Tether.

sections.heading: Source speed is not Arbiscan's clock
sections.body: Chain id 56 can move in about 3 seconds. That fact does not time the bridge and does not lock a price. Read the minimum USDT. Sign only on BNB Chain. When you look for the tokens, the wallet has to be on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, and it has to hold ETH.

faqs.question: Why does the BNB address look like an ETH marker?
faqs.answer: Routers use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for the gas coin in front of you. On BNB Chain that is BNB, and BscScan shows a native send. The payout is not that marker. It is Tether, 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, on Arbiscan, chain id 42161. There is no ERC-20 approval on the BNB. Nova is a different chain.

faqs.question: Does this USDT use 18 decimals like the BNB Chain peg?
faqs.answer: Read the quote rather than a raw integer. This page pays Arbitrum One Tether, and it is not spending the 18-decimal USDT peg on BNB Chain. You still need ETH on chain id 42161 to move the tokens. The ARB token will not cover that fee. Arbiscan is the check.

faqs.question: What if the quote says USDT and I needed USDC?
faqs.answer: Do not sign. This route pays Tether only, contract 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Native USDC is a different page from the same BNB balance. Treating them as the same dollar is the wrong tool. Check Arbiscan before you send the tokens onward. Look again.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive native ETH on Arbitrum One. The same marker is a different gas coin on each chain. Check BscScan and Arbiscan.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to ETH on Arbitrum One. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive native ETH on Arbitrum One, not on Nova.

Both sides use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On BNB Chain, chain id 56, the marker is BNB. On Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, it is ETH. BscScan shows the BNB leaving. Arbiscan shows the ETH arriving. There is no ERC-20 approval on either gas coin. Blocks on BNB Chain are about 3 seconds. This is not WETH, not the ETH peg, and not the ARB token.

sections.heading: Same marker, BNB out and ETH in
sections.body: The string is not one coin hopping chains. It means the gas coin of the chain you are on. You sell BNB and you buy ETH. Both can move. The Binance-Peg ETH contract is not an input. If that is all you hold, this page will not take it. Leave some BNB or the source fee fails.

sections.heading: The ETH you receive can pay Arbitrum fees
sections.body: Because the payout is the gas coin, you do not need old ETH on Arbitrum One for the new balance to be usable. That is the difference from landing in USDC, USDT, WETH, or ARB. Arbiscan will not show an ERC-20 for this credit. Nova will not show it either.

sections.heading: WETH and ARB if you did not want the gas coin
sections.body: Those payouts are other pages from the same BNB. This one is the wrong tool if a pool asked for the WETH contract or if you wanted the ARB token. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the wait, not a BNB to ETH rate. Nothing freezes the amount.

sections.heading: Read the ETH floor on two moving coins
sections.body: The estimate and the minimum are different lines. Sign against the minimum. A 3 second block on chain id 56 does not freeze ETH. Confirm the wallet is on BNB Chain before the signature, then look on Arbiscan with chain id 42161. If the floor is too small, do not sign.

faqs.question: Why are both addresses identical if BNB and ETH differ?
faqs.answer: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE stands in for the native gas coin. BscScan's native coin on chain id 56 is BNB. Arbiscan's native coin on chain id 42161 is ETH. There is no ERC-20 approval on either side. The ETH peg and the ARB token are separate assets and are not this route. Nova is not the destination.

faqs.question: Do I need ETH on Arbitrum before this swap?
faqs.answer: No. The ETH from this route can pay fees after it arrives. You do need BNB left on chain id 56 to pay the source fee. If you spend the entire BNB balance, the send cannot be mined. Arbiscan is where the native credit belongs, on Arbitrum One, not Nova.

faqs.question: Can I undo it if ETH drops after BscScan confirms?
faqs.answer: No. A confirmed BNB transfer is not reversed here, and the price is not insured. Read the minimum ETH first. The 3 second block is only BNB Chain. It is not a promise about how much ETH Arbiscan will show, or about when that credit appears.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive WETH on Arbitrum One. WETH cannot pay gas. Match the Arbitrum WETH contract on Arbiscan before you sign the swap.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to WETH on Arbitrum One. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive WETH on Arbitrum One, not native ETH and not on Nova.

The BNB side is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin on chain id 56. No ERC-20 approval. BscScan shows the native send. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Leave BNB for the fee. Arbitrum WETH is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Match it on Arbiscan, chain id 42161. It is not mainnet WETH and not the BNB Chain ETH peg. You still need native ETH on Arbitrum One to move the wrapper.

sections.heading: Selling BNB for a wrapper, not for gas
sections.body: Native BNB is the input. The peg at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is not. If your ether exposure on BNB Chain is only that peg, this page cannot see it. There is no approval for BNB, but the fee still comes out of BNB. Do not zero the balance and expect the swap to pass.

sections.heading: This wrapper cannot pay Arbitrum One
sections.body: 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 is an ERC-20. ETH is the native coin. Arbiscan lists them apart. Receiving WETH does not give you ETH, so a new wallet gets a token it cannot move. Mainnet WETH will not update. Nova will not show the balance. ARB will not pay the fee.

sections.heading: Open the ETH page if you needed gas
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the point was a spendable Arbitrum balance. USDC, USDT, and ARB pages are the wrong tool when you wanted those tokens instead. [How bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) covers the wait between BscScan and Arbiscan. It does not promise a WETH amount.

sections.heading: Minimum WETH, leftover BNB, ETH already there
sections.body: Three checks: the minimum WETH on the quote, the BNB you keep for chain id 56, and the ETH already on chain id 42161. A 3 second source block does not replace any of them. Sign only if the WETH floor is acceptable. If the quote expired, price it again.

faqs.question: Will Arbitrum WETH show up as ETH in the wallet?
faqs.answer: No. ETH is the gas coin. WETH is the token at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbiscan, chain id 42161. The BNB you sent was the marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on BscScan. They stay different. You need ETH already if you want to transfer the wrapper. Nova is not the network.

faqs.question: Is this the same WETH address Ethereum mainnet uses?
faqs.answer: No. Mainnet WETH is a different contract. This payout is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One. Matching the ticker is not enough. You also need BNB left over for the source fee. There is no ERC-20 approval on the BNB itself. Arbiscan is the explorer to use.

faqs.question: What if the only ether I hold is the BNB Chain peg?
faqs.answer: This page will not spend it. The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and has its own route to Arbitrum WETH. You need native BNB here, both to sell and to pay gas. If BscScan shows only dust BNB, the route cannot start. Open the peg page instead.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive ARB on Arbitrum One. ARB does not pay gas. You still need ETH. Match the ARB contract on Arbiscan before you sign.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to ARB on Arbitrum One. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive the ARB token on Arbitrum One.

The BNB side is the marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin on chain id 56. No ERC-20 approval. BscScan shows the native send. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Leave BNB for the fee. ARB is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Match it on Arbiscan, chain id 42161, not Nova. ARB cannot pay gas. ETH has to be in the receiving wallet or the token cannot move. This is not WETH and not a dollar token.

sections.heading: Native BNB buys the governance token
sections.body: You sell BNB and you buy ARB. The ETH peg is not the input. A stablecoin peg is not the input. There is no approval on BNB, but the fee still requires a remainder. If you drain BNB, the send never starts and no ARB is created. The trade takes ARB price risk the whole time the route is open.

sections.heading: ARB on One still needs ETH beside it
sections.body: 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is not the gas coin. Arbiscan lists ETH separately. A wallet that receives ARB with no ETH can see the token and still fail a transfer. Nova will not show this balance. The ARB ticker does not substitute for chain id 42161 gas.

sections.heading: ETH and dollar pages if ARB was the wrong ask
sections.body: Native ETH can pay fees after it arrives, and that is a different page. Native USDC and USDT are different pages. WETH is different again. The [bridge guide](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the hop, not an ARB price. Stay on BNB Chain if you did not need this token.

sections.heading: Fee remainder, ARB floor, ETH already waiting
sections.body: Keep BNB for chain id 56. Read the minimum ARB. Confirm ETH is already on Arbitrum One. A 3 second source block does not deliver any of those three. Sign only on BNB Chain. Look up 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbiscan after, on chain id 42161.

faqs.question: Does this route pay ETH as well as ARB?
faqs.answer: No. It pays the ARB token at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 only. ETH is what you must already hold on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, to move that token. The BNB you send is the marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on BscScan. There is no ERC-20 approval on it. Nova is not the destination.

faqs.question: Can ARB pay the Arbitrum fee after it arrives?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on Arbitrum One is ETH. ARB is a separate token, and Arbiscan shows it that way. If the wallet has ARB and no ETH, you still cannot send it. BNB left on BNB Chain does not cover the gap. Add ETH first. This page does not mint that ETH for you.

faqs.question: What if I wanted native ETH and opened the ARB page?
faqs.answer: Leave it unsigned. This route pays ARB, not the gas coin. The native ETH page uses the gas-coin marker as the payout and a different quote. Signing here sells BNB into the governance token. If that is not what you meant to hold, it is the wrong tool.

description: Send Binance-Peg USDC from BNB Chain and receive native ETH on Base. Base is an L2 and gas is ETH. Check BscScan and Basescan before you sign the quote.
intro:
Swap USDC from BNB Chain to ETH on Base. You send Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain and you receive native ETH on Base, the coin that pays gas on that L2.

Approve 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. BscScan lists the 18-decimal peg on chain id 56. Gas is BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. The payout marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means ETH on Base, not BNB and not WETH. Basescan shows the native balance. Chain id 8453. Base is an Ethereum L2, not Ethereum mainnet. The ETH you receive can pay later fees.

sections.heading: A peg dollar buys Base's gas coin
sections.body: You sell 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d and take ETH exposure. USDT and WETH are different pages. If you wanted a dollar token on Base, this payout is the wrong tool. Keep BNB so the approval can be mined. Read the quote instead of the raw 18-decimal integer on BscScan.

sections.heading: The marker means ETH on chain id 8453
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not an ERC-20 on Basescan. On Base it means native ETH. The same string on BNB Chain would mean BNB, which is not the input. This ETH can pay L2 gas. It is not mainnet ETH sitting on chain id 1, and Etherscan will not show the credit.

sections.heading: WETH is a predeploy, not this payout
sections.body: Base WETH uses 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, and that is a different page. If a pool wants the wrapper, do not sign here. [Base](/chains/base) is the L2 you are funding. The quote does not lock an ETH amount. A 3 second BNB Chain block is not a delivery clock.

sections.heading: A fresh Base wallet can spend this ETH
sections.body: The payout is the gas coin, so a fresh Base wallet can use it once it arrives. You still need BNB on chain id 56. Read the minimum ETH before you sign. Confirm the wallet network is Base, chain id 8453, on Basescan, not Ethereum mainnet. Mainnet ETH is a different balance.

faqs.question: Does the long placeholder mean I am sending BNB?
faqs.answer: No. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is the destination, and on Base it means native ETH. You approve Binance-Peg USDC, 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, on BscScan. Gas for that approval is BNB. Basescan should later show ETH on chain id 8453. Base is an L2, not Ethereum mainnet.

faqs.question: Will I get the Base WETH predeploy instead?
faqs.answer: No. This page pays native ETH, which can pay gas. WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is a different route. If a contract on Base demands that predeploy, leave this quote. You still pay BNB on the way out. The received ETH is not a mainnet balance.

faqs.question: Is the ETH amount fixed when BNB Chain confirms?
faqs.answer: No. Blocks near 3 seconds are only the source. ETH can move while the bridge is open, and this page does not promise a price or a completion time. Judge the minimum ETH. If it is too small for the peg you are selling, do not sign.

description: Send Binance-Peg USDC from BNB Chain and receive WETH on Base. The predeploy is not mainnet WETH and cannot pay gas. Check BscScan and Basescan. Keep ETH.
intro:
Swap USDC from BNB Chain to WETH on Base. You send Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain and you receive WETH on Base, not native ETH.

The peg is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, 18 decimals. Approve it. BscScan shows it on chain id 56, gas in BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. Base WETH is the predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Match it on Basescan, chain id 8453. That address is not Ethereum mainnet WETH. Base is an L2. Gas is ETH. This wrapper cannot pay it.

sections.heading: The peg buys Base's wrapper
sections.body: Only 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d is spent. You leave a dollar token and take wrapped ether exposure on an L2. If you wanted native ETH that can pay gas, this page is the wrong tool. Keep BNB for the approval. The raw peg integer is not the price on the quote.

sections.heading: 0x4200 is Base WETH, not a shared mainnet token
sections.body: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is the WETH predeploy on Base. The same shape of address exists on other rollups, but this page settles on Base only, chain id 8453. Basescan is the explorer. Etherscan will not show the balance. Without native ETH already in the wallet, the wrapper sits still.

sections.heading: Native ETH is the fee page
sections.body: Open that page if you need gas. Open a USDT page if you need Tether. Stay on BNB Chain if Base was never required. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is only the source. The quote does not freeze a WETH amount, and the source block time is not a Basescan promise.

sections.heading: ETH has to be on Base already
sections.body: Read the minimum WETH, then check chain id 8453 for a native ETH balance. Without it you cannot move the predeploy and you cannot unwrap it. Sign on BNB Chain only. If the floor is thin, do not sign. Other rollups reuse the predeploy shape. Only Basescan on chain id 8453 counts for this page. Check it there.

faqs.question: Can I look up this WETH on Ethereum mainnet?
faqs.answer: No. Base WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Basescan, chain id 8453. Mainnet WETH is a different contract on Etherscan. The peg you send is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan. Gas on Base is ETH, and this wrapper cannot pay it. Base is an L2, not chain id 1.

faqs.question: Does the wrapper arrive with ETH for gas?
faqs.answer: No. The route pays WETH only. ETH is a separate native balance on Base. If the wallet has none, the predeploy is visible and stuck. BNB you kept on BNB Chain does not become that ETH. Add ETH on chain id 8453 before you need to use the wrapper.

faqs.question: What if I needed native ETH on Base instead?
faqs.answer: Then this page is the wrong tool. It sells the USDC peg for the wrapper, which cannot pay gas. The native ETH page uses the gas-coin marker as the payout. Leave this quote unsigned if the point was fee money. The source gas is still BNB.

description: Send Binance-Peg USDT from BNB Chain and receive Circle USDC on Base. You change issuer and chain. Match both contracts on BscScan and Basescan before you sign.
intro:
Swap USDT from BNB Chain to USDC on Base. You send Binance-Peg USDT on BNB Chain and you receive Circle USDC on Base.

Approve 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, the 18-decimal Tether peg. BscScan shows it on chain id 56. Gas is BNB. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Circle USDC on Base is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Match it on Basescan. Chain id 8453. Base is an Ethereum L2, not mainnet, so this is not Ethereum USDC. Gas after arrival is ETH. USDC will not pay it.

sections.heading: Tether's peg is the only approval
sections.body: 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 is the input. The USDC peg and native BNB are different routes. You change issuer, from Tether to Circle, and you land on an L2. If you needed Tether to stay Tether, this page is the wrong tool. Keep BNB for the fee. Do not compare raw 18-decimal and 6-decimal integers.

sections.heading: Base USDC is Circle's contract on Basescan
sections.body: 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 is the payout. It is not Ethereum mainnet USDC and not the BNB Chain peg. Basescan is the check, chain id 8453. ETH has to sit in the wallet or the USDC cannot move. Etherscan will not update when this L2 balance arrives.

sections.heading: ETH and WETH are other endings
sections.body: Each has a page from this same peg. This page is only Circle USDC. A local swap on BNB Chain is enough when Base was not required. [Base](/chains/base) is the L2, chain id 8453. The quote does not lock the Circle dollars and does not name a finish time.

sections.heading: Issuer change, then an ETH fee
sections.body: BscScan proves the peg left. Basescan proves the USDC arrived. BNB pays the first side. ETH pays the second, on the L2. Read the minimum USDC before you sign. A 3 second block is not the whole route. If the floor is short, do not sign. Base remains an L2, chain id 8453, not mainnet.

faqs.question: Is Base USDC the same contract as Ethereum USDC?
faqs.answer: No. This payout is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan, chain id 8453. Ethereum USDC is a mainnet contract on Etherscan. The input was the Tether peg 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan. You need ETH on Base afterward. Base is an L2, so a mainnet wallet view will not show the tokens.

faqs.question: Does the route keep me in Tether?
faqs.answer: No. You sell Tether's peg and receive Circle USDC. If a desk asked for Tether on Base, this is the wrong tool. BscScan and Basescan will not show one shared balance. Gas out is BNB on chain id 56. Gas on Base is ETH, and USDC cannot pay it.

faqs.question: Can I move the USDC if the Base wallet has no ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 does not pay L2 gas. ETH does, on chain id 8453. Basescan can show the token while a transfer fails. BNB left on BNB Chain does not help. Add ETH on Base first. Then try again.

description: Send Binance-Peg USDT from BNB Chain and receive native ETH on Base. You leave Tether for the L2 gas coin. Check BscScan and Basescan before you sign.
intro:
Swap USDT from BNB Chain to ETH on Base. You send Binance-Peg USDT on BNB Chain and you receive native ETH on Base.

The peg is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, 18 decimals. Approve it. BscScan is the explorer, chain id 56, gas in BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. The payout marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means ETH on Base. Basescan shows that native balance. Chain id 8453. Base is an L2, not mainnet. This is not WETH. The ETH you receive can pay later fees on Base.

sections.heading: Selling the Tether peg for L2 ETH
sections.body: The input is only 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. The USDC peg will not be pulled. You leave a dollar token and take ETH exposure. If you wanted Circle USDC or WETH, this page is the wrong tool. Keep BNB for the approval. The raw peg amount is not a price.

sections.heading: Native ETH on Base, not on mainnet
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not a token page on Basescan. On chain id 8453 it means the gas coin. That ETH can pay L2 fees, so you do not need a prior ETH balance for the credit to be usable. Etherscan will not show it as a mainnet balance. WETH is the predeploy, a different route.

sections.heading: Dollar pages if you did not want ETH risk
sections.body: Circle USDC is a different ending from this same peg. Staying on BNB Chain is smaller when you only needed to exit USDT into BNB. [How bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the wait onto the L2. No ETH price is guaranteed. The 3 second block is not a completion time.

sections.heading: Leave BNB and accept a minimum in ETH
sections.body: Do not spend the last BNB on a larger peg balance. Read the minimum ETH before you sign on chain id 56. Then look for a native balance on Basescan, chain id 8453. If the wallet is on Ethereum mainnet, you are on the wrong network. Switch it to Base before you look.

faqs.question: Does this ETH land on Ethereum mainnet?
faqs.answer: No. It lands on Base, chain id 8453, which is an L2. Basescan shows it. The marker is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, meaning native ETH on Base, not WETH. You approve 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan and pay BNB. Etherscan will not show this as a chain id 1 balance.

faqs.question: Is the payout the WETH predeploy?
faqs.answer: No. WETH on Base is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 and cannot pay gas until you already have ETH. This page pays the gas coin itself. If a contract wants the predeploy, you are on the wrong route. BscScan is only the source side.

faqs.question: Can the amount change after the peg leaves BNB Chain?
faqs.answer: The source block is about 3 seconds. That is not the whole route, and ETH can move while the bridge is open. This page does not promise a price or a completion time. The minimum ETH is what you accept or reject. Refresh when the quote expires.

description: Send Binance-Peg USDT from BNB Chain and receive WETH on Base. The predeploy cannot pay gas. Match the peg on BscScan and the WETH address on Basescan.
intro:
Swap USDT from BNB Chain to WETH on Base. You send Binance-Peg USDT on BNB Chain and you receive WETH on Base.

Approve 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. BscScan lists that 18-decimal peg on chain id 56. Gas is BNB. Blocks are about 3 seconds. WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Match it on Basescan, chain id 8453. Base is an L2. That predeploy is not mainnet WETH. The wrapper cannot pay gas. ETH has to be on Base already.

sections.heading: Tether's peg in, the Base predeploy out
sections.body: The contract you approve is only 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. You are not spending BNB and you are not spending the USDC peg. The result is WETH, so you take ether price risk. If you wanted native ETH or Circle USDC, stop. The approval spends BNB and does not credit Basescan by itself.

sections.heading: This 0x4200 address is Base only on this page
sections.body: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 will not match Ethereum's WETH page on Etherscan. Other rollups reuse the same predeploy shape. This route is Base, chain id 8453, on Basescan. Without native ETH there, the wrapper cannot move and cannot be unwrapped. The USDT peg did not pay that ETH.

sections.heading: Open the native ETH page for fees
sections.body: Fee money is the gas coin, not this contract. Circle USDC is the dollar payout. [How to bridge](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) explains the hop onto the L2. It is not a locked WETH price. If you never needed Base, sell the peg on BNB Chain.

sections.heading: BNB, ETH, and a WETH floor
sections.body: BNB on chain id 56 for the send. ETH on chain id 8453 for the next transaction. A minimum WETH you still accept. A 3 second source block does not supply the missing ETH. Sign only if that floor is enough. Recheck the predeploy if any character looks off. Another rollup can share the shape of that address and still not be Base. Chain id 8453 is the only match.

faqs.question: Will this WETH show up as spendable ETH on Base?
faqs.answer: No. Wallets list 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 apart from native ETH. Basescan does the same on chain id 8453. The peg you sent was 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan. If you needed fee ETH, use the native ETH route. Base is an L2, not Ethereum mainnet.

faqs.question: Do I approve the predeploy before the WETH arrives?
faqs.answer: No. The first approval is for the BNB Chain peg, and it spends BNB. The predeploy may need an approval later, when a pool asks for it, and that later approval spends ETH you must already hold on Base. This page does not pre-approve anything on chain id 8453.

faqs.question: What if I hold the USDC peg instead of this USDT?
faqs.answer: This page will not take it. The USDC peg has its own route to Base WETH. Approving the wrong contract does not start the swap. Check 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan. The payout stays the predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 only on this route. Check the peg.

description: Send Binance-Peg ETH from BNB Chain and receive Circle USDC on Base. The peg is not BNB. Match both contracts on BscScan and Basescan before you sign.
intro:
Swap ETH from BNB Chain to USDC on Base. You send Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain and you receive Circle USDC on Base.

The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. You approve it. BscScan shows it on chain id 56. It is not BNB and not native ETH. Gas is BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. Circle USDC on Base is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Match it on Basescan, chain id 8453. Base is an L2, not mainnet. ETH pays gas there. USDC does not.

sections.heading: An ETH label that still needs BNB
sections.body: Wallets call 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 ETH. The fee coin is BNB. This page spends the peg only. If you hold BNB and no peg, the approval finds nothing. Native ETH already on Base is not an input. Keep BNB or chain id 56 never broadcasts.

sections.heading: Circle on Basescan, then an ETH gap
sections.body: 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 is Base USDC, not mainnet USDC and not Tether. Six decimals look small next to the 18-decimal peg. Use the quote. Then hold ETH on chain id 8453, because the USDC cannot pay L2 gas. Etherscan will not show this balance.

sections.heading: BNB, native ETH, and WETH are other jobs
sections.body: Spending BNB is another page. Receiving native ETH or the WETH predeploy is another page. This one is peg in, Circle USDC out. [Base](/chains/base) is the L2. If you did not need chain id 8453, trade on BNB Chain. The quote does not lock the USDC.

sections.heading: Read the USDC floor before you approve
sections.body: The approval costs BNB and does not freeze the quote. Read the minimum USDC when you sign the swap. A 3 second block is only BNB Chain. It is not a promise that Basescan shows the token. Sign on chain id 56. Ignore a destination from a message. Etherscan will stay quiet because this USDC is an L2 balance on Base, and you still need ETH there to move it later.

faqs.question: Is the BNB Chain ETH peg the same as Base gas?
faqs.answer: No. The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. Gas on Base is native ETH, chain id 8453, and this page does not pay it. It pays Circle USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan. You need BNB to send and ETH after arrival. Base is an L2, not mainnet.

faqs.question: Will Etherscan show this USDC?
faqs.answer: No. Etherscan is mainnet. This USDC is on Base, and Basescan is the explorer. If you only check chain id 1, the balance looks missing. The source peg is still 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Switch the wallet to chain id 8453, and keep ETH there so the USDC can move.

faqs.question: Why can the USDC not be sent after it appears?
faqs.answer: The Base wallet is missing ETH. Circle USDC does not pay gas on chain id 8453. Basescan can show the token anyway. BNB left on BNB Chain cannot pay that L2 fee. Add ETH, then the transfer can be signed. This page does not include ETH in the payout.

description: Send Binance-Peg ETH from BNB Chain and receive WETH on Base. The peg and the predeploy are different. WETH cannot pay gas. Check BscScan and Basescan.
intro:
Swap ETH from BNB Chain to WETH on Base. You send Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain and you receive WETH on Base.

The source is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Approve it on BscScan, chain id 56, gas in BNB, blocks about 3 seconds. Base WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Match it on Basescan. It is not the peg, not native ETH, and not mainnet WETH. Chain id 8453. Base is an L2. Gas is ETH. The wrapper cannot pay that gas.

sections.heading: Peg in, predeploy out
sections.body: This page spends only 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. It does not spend BNB, and it does not wrap ETH that already sits on Base. If the peg balance is empty, there is nothing to approve. Keep BNB for gas on chain id 56. Both assets get called ether. The contracts do not match.

sections.heading: The predeploy still needs native ETH
sections.body: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 arriving does not top up ETH. Basescan shows a token, not a native credit. Every later move costs ETH on chain id 8453. A fresh wallet can display WETH and still fail a transfer. BNB left behind does not become that ETH. Etherscan will not show it.

sections.heading: Native ETH is the gas landing
sections.body: If you wanted spendable gas, this wrapper is the wrong tool. Circle USDC is the wrong tool if you wanted dollars. [How bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the wait onto the L2. No WETH amount is promised. Other rollups share this predeploy shape. This page is Base only.

sections.heading: Do not drain BNB to buy more peg
sections.body: The fee and the trade are different balances. Draining BNB stalls the approval. Read the minimum WETH before you sign on chain id 56. A 3 second block is not a Basescan timestamp. If the floor is too small, leave the quote unsigned. Other rollups reuse this predeploy shape, and only chain id 8453 is this page at all today.

faqs.question: Are the peg and Base WETH the same token?
faqs.answer: No. The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. Base WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Basescan, chain id 8453. Mainnet WETH is a third contract. This page pays the Base predeploy only. You need BNB to send and ETH to move the result. Base is an L2.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap the predeploy without holding ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Unwrapping stays on Base and the fee is native ETH. This route does not include that unwrap. If your goal was the gas coin, open the native ETH page before you sign. A wallet that receives only the predeploy cannot pay for its own unwrap.

faqs.question: What if I meant to send BNB, not the peg?
faqs.answer: Stop. BNB is the gas coin and has its own route to Base WETH. Approving 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 will not spend BNB. Check the native balance on BscScan. This page is the wrong tool for a BNB sale, even when the payout is also called ether.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive Circle USDC on Base. No approval on the BNB. Match the USDC contract on Basescan and keep ETH on Base for gas.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to USDC on Base. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive Circle USDC on Base.

The source marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means BNB, the gas coin on chain id 56. No ERC-20 approval. BscScan shows a native send. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Leave extra BNB for the fee. Circle USDC on Base is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Match it on Basescan, chain id 8453. Base is an L2, not mainnet. You will need ETH there to move the USDC.

sections.heading: BNB pays the fee and is the asset
sections.body: There is no token approval, but there is a fee. Selling every BNB stalls the transaction. The page will not sell the ETH peg and will not sell a stablecoin peg. If those are the balances you meant, this is the wrong route. The marker is the gas coin, not a token page on BscScan.

sections.heading: Circle on the L2, ETH still required
sections.body: Basescan should show 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. It is not mainnet USDC. The token cannot pay gas on chain id 8453. ETH has to be there already. BNB does not arrive with the dollars. Etherscan will not list this L2 balance.

sections.heading: The peg is not pulled into this swap
sections.body: The ETH listing on BNB Chain is a peg this page ignores. Native ETH and WETH payouts are different pages. [Base](/chains/base) is the destination L2. If you only needed USDC on BNB Chain, do not bridge. No Circle amount is locked.

sections.heading: Split the BNB, then read the floor
sections.body: Keep a fee remainder, then read the minimum USDC. A 3 second block on chain id 56 is not a promise that Basescan has the token. Sign while the wallet says BNB Chain. Look for the result on chain id 8453. Reject destinations you did not generate. ETH on Base is still required after the USDC shows up, because the token cannot pay L2 gas.

faqs.question: Do I approve BNB before this Base USDC swap?
faqs.answer: No. Native BNB uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which is not an ERC-20. BscScan shows a native transfer on chain id 56. You only leave extra BNB for gas. The USDC you receive is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan. That token needs ETH on Base, chain id 8453, before it can move.

faqs.question: Is this USDC visible on Ethereum mainnet?
faqs.answer: No. Base is an L2. Basescan is the explorer, not Etherscan. Chain id 8453 will not appear as a mainnet token balance. If you are still on chain id 1 in the wallet, switch. You also need ETH on Base. BNB paid only the source side.

faqs.question: What if I spend the last of my BNB?
faqs.answer: The fee comes from the same native balance you are selling. Leave enough BNB on chain id 56 or the send cannot be mined and no USDC appears on Base. This page also does not promise a price or a completion time once a valid send does go through.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive native ETH on Base. The same marker is a different gas coin on each side. Check BscScan and Basescan before you sign.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to ETH on Base. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive native ETH on Base.

Both sides use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On BNB Chain, chain id 56, the marker is BNB. On Base, chain id 8453, it is ETH. BscScan shows the BNB leaving. Basescan shows the ETH arriving. There is no ERC-20 approval on either gas coin. Blocks on BNB Chain are about 3 seconds. Base is an Ethereum L2, not mainnet. This is not the WETH predeploy and not the ETH peg.

sections.heading: One marker, BNB leaving and ETH arriving
sections.body: The string is not a coin that teleports. It means the gas coin of the chain you are on. You sell BNB and you buy ETH on an L2. Both can move. The Binance-Peg ETH contract is not an input. If that is all you hold, this page will not take it. Leave some BNB or the source fee fails.

sections.heading: Received ETH can pay Base fees
sections.body: Because the payout is the gas coin, you do not need old ETH on Base for the new balance to be usable. That differs from landing in USDC or WETH. Basescan will not show an ERC-20 for this credit. Etherscan will not show it as mainnet ETH. Chain id 8453 is the check.

sections.heading: The predeploy if you needed the wrapper
sections.body: WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is another page. This one is the wrong tool if a pool asked for that contract. Dollar payouts are other pages too. [How bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the wait, not a BNB to ETH rate. Nothing freezes the amount.

sections.heading: Read the ETH floor before you sign
sections.body: The estimate and the minimum are different lines. Sign against the minimum. A 3 second block on chain id 56 does not freeze ETH. Confirm the wallet is on BNB Chain, then look on Basescan with chain id 8453. If the floor is too small, do not sign.

faqs.question: Why do both addresses match if BNB and ETH differ?
faqs.answer: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE stands in for the native gas coin. BscScan's native coin on chain id 56 is BNB. Basescan's native coin on chain id 8453 is ETH. There is no ERC-20 approval on either side. The ETH peg and the WETH predeploy are separate. Base is an L2, not Ethereum mainnet.

faqs.question: Do I need ETH on Base before this swap?
faqs.answer: No. The ETH from this route can pay L2 fees after it arrives. You do need BNB left on chain id 56 to pay the source fee. If you spend the entire BNB balance, the send cannot be mined. Basescan is where the native credit belongs, on chain id 8453.

faqs.question: Can I reverse it if ETH drops after I sign?
faqs.answer: No. A confirmed BNB transfer is not reversed here, and the price is not insured. Read the minimum ETH first. The 3 second block is only BNB Chain. It is not a promise about how much ETH Basescan will show, or about when that credit appears.

description: Send native BNB from BNB Chain and receive WETH on Base. The predeploy cannot pay gas. Match 0x4200 on Basescan and keep ETH on Base before you sign it.
intro:
Swap BNB from BNB Chain to WETH on Base. You send native BNB on BNB Chain and you receive WETH on Base, not native ETH.

The BNB side is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin on chain id 56. No ERC-20 approval. BscScan shows the native send. Blocks are about 3 seconds. Leave BNB for the fee. Base WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Match it on Basescan, chain id 8453. It is not mainnet WETH and not the BNB Chain ETH peg. Base is an L2. You still need native ETH on Base to move the wrapper.

sections.heading: Selling BNB for the predeploy
sections.body: Native BNB is the input. The peg at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 is not. If your ether exposure on BNB Chain is only that peg, this page cannot see it. There is no approval for BNB, but the fee still comes out of BNB. Do not zero the balance and expect the swap to pass.

sections.heading: The predeploy cannot pay the L2
sections.body: 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 is an ERC-20 on Base. ETH is the native coin. Basescan lists them apart. Receiving WETH does not give you ETH, so a new wallet gets a token it cannot move. Mainnet WETH will not update. The same address shape on another rollup is not this balance.

sections.heading: Native ETH on Base if you needed gas
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the point was a spendable Base balance. USDC is the wrong tool when you wanted Circle's dollar token. [How to bridge assets](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) covers the hop from BscScan to Basescan. It does not promise a WETH amount.

sections.heading: Three checks before the wrapper is useful
sections.body: The minimum WETH on the quote, the BNB you keep for chain id 56, and the ETH already on chain id 8453. A 3 second source block does not replace any of them. Sign only if the WETH floor is acceptable. If the quote expired, price it again.

faqs.question: Will Base WETH show up as ETH in the wallet?
faqs.answer: No. ETH is the gas coin. WETH is the predeploy 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Basescan, chain id 8453. The BNB you sent was the marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on BscScan. They stay different. You need ETH already if you want to transfer the wrapper. Base is an L2, not mainnet.

faqs.question: Is 0x4200 the Ethereum mainnet WETH address?
faqs.answer: No. Mainnet WETH is a different contract on Etherscan. This payout is the Base predeploy, and other rollups can share the same address shape. This page is chain id 8453 only. You also need BNB left for the source fee. There is no ERC-20 approval on the BNB. Basescan is the explorer.

faqs.question: What if I only hold the ETH peg on BNB Chain?
faqs.answer: This page will not spend it. The peg is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and has its own route to Base WETH. You need native BNB here, both to sell and to pay gas. If BscScan shows only dust BNB, the route cannot start. Open the peg page instead.

description: Send Binance-Peg USDC from BNB Chain and receive Tether USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Gas there is AVAX, not the X-Chain. Match both contracts before you sign.

sections.heading: You sell BNB, not the ETH peg
sections.body: This page takes native BNB only. The ETH peg and the USDT peg on BNB Chain stay put. There is no approval step for BNB. You still cannot spend the last BNB, because the network fee has to fit in the remainder. If the balance you meant was the peg, open that page instead of this one.

sections.heading: Tether on C-Chain is not Ethereum Tether
sections.body: Match 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Snowtrace. Etherscan will not show this payout, and the X-Chain will not either. It is Tether, not Circle's native USDC. The token does not include AVAX. Add AVAX on chain id 43114 or the USDT sits where it cannot be transferred.

sections.heading: USDC and AVAX if Tether was not the ask
sections.body: Circle's native USDC is a different contract. AVAX is the gas-coin payout, a different page. The ETH peg is a different input. If you wanted USDT without leaving BNB Chain, buy it there. [Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) is C-Chain only. The quote does not freeze the Tether amount.

sections.heading: A 3 second block is not Snowtrace's clock
sections.body: Chain id 56 can move in about 3 seconds. That fact does not time the bridge and does not lock a price. Read the minimum USDT. Sign only on BNB Chain. When you look for the tokens, the wallet has to be on C-Chain, chain id 43114, and it has to hold AVAX.

faqs.question: Why does the BNB address look like other gas-coin markers?
faqs.answer: Routers use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for the gas coin in front of you. On BNB Chain that is BNB, and BscScan shows a native send. The payout is not that marker. It is Tether, 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, on Snowtrace, chain id 43114. There is no ERC-20 approval on the BNB. The X-Chain is a different chain.

faqs.question: Does this USDT use 18 decimals like BNB Chain USDT?
faqs.answer: Read the quote rather than a raw integer. This page pays C-Chain Tether, and it is not spending the 18-decimal USDT peg on BNB Chain. You still need AVAX on chain id 43114 to move the tokens. Snowtrace is the check. An X-Chain balance will not pay that fee.

faqs.question: What if the quote says USDT and I needed USDC?
faqs.answer: Do not sign. This route pays Tether only, contract 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Native USDC is a different page from the same BNB balance. Treating them as the same dollar is the wrong tool. Check Snowtrace before you send the tokens onward. Look twice.
